InsideOfTruck_EventScript_SetIntroFlags.reason: The gender branch of the truck's exit-tile trigger, ported as its flag/var effect: assets::new_game_flags::TRUCK_INTRO_FLAGS_MALE/_FEMALE (5 setflags each) and TRUCK_INTRO_VARS_MALE/_FEMALE (VAR_LITTLEROOT_INTRO_STATE, VAR_LITTLEROOT_HOUSES_STATE_BRENDAN/_MAY), applied by crate::new_game::apply_truck_intro_flags at new-game init. Upstream this is a coord (trigger) event on all three truck exit tiles gated on VAR_LITTLEROOT_INTRO_STATE == 0 (data/maps/InsideOfTruck/map.json:85-112), so it fires exactly once on the way out of the truck and every real playthrough passes through it before reaching a house; this port skips the truck sequence entirely, so new-game init is the point the skipped flow would have produced the effect -- same 'the effect, without an interpreter' shape as the EventScript_ResetAllMapFlags application beside it. Load-bearing rather than cosmetic now that object-event visibility gates collision and rendering (issue #161): without it a fresh save reaches the player's house with the rival's Poke Ball spawned in the bedroom as an invisible collider and the rival's mother and sibling spawned in the player's own 1F (a duplicated mother plus another undrawn blocker). The two branches are exact Brendan/May mirrors, and a playerGender byte outside MALE/FEMALE applies neither, matching the script's own missing else. As of issue #261, the leading setrespawn HEAL_LOCATION_LITTLEROOT_TOWN_{BRENDANS,MAYS}_HOUSE_2F line IS modelled too -- crate::new_game::default_last_heal_location reproduces its SetLastHealLocationWarp effect (gender-branched, same fallback-to-no-op for an out-of-range gender byte), applied to SaveBlock1::last_heal_location alongside this artifact's own flags/vars at init_save_blocks time; see src/overworld.c#SetLastHealLocationWarp for the full citation. Still not modelled: setdynamicwarp MAP_LITTLEROOT_TOWN (no dynamic-warp destination state), the lockall/releaseall pair, and setflag FLAG_HIDE_MAP_NAME_POPUP (outside both gender branches; no map-name popup is rendered). The rest of this file -- InsideOfTruck_OnLoad's setmetatile calls, InsideOfTruck_OnResume's STEP_CB_TRUCK step callback, and the moving-box sign -- is untouched: the truck map itself is not bundled.

SecretBase_EventScript_SetDecorationFlag.reason: The 14 setflag FLAG_DECORATION_1..14 commands, ported as their effect: crate::flow::overworld_phase::run_on_transition_map_script applies assets::object_event_flags::DECORATION_FLAGS on entering either bundled player bedroom, the two maps whose own MAP_SCRIPT_ON_TRANSITION calls this script (LittlerootTown_{Brendans,Mays}House_2F/scripts.inc:6-12). Same 'the effect, without an interpreter' shape as new_game's partial port of EventScript_ResetAllMapFlags. Required for correctness, not cosmetics: decoration placeholders invert the usual polarity (an EMPTY slot is the flag-SET state), nothing sets these at new-game time (InitEventData zeroes all flags; EventScript_ResetAllMapFlags never mentions them), and upstream relies purely on ordering -- RunOnTransitionMapScript (overworld.c:860) precedes TrySpawnObjectEvents (overworld.c:2163-2178) -- so without it a fresh save reads all twelve bedroom placeholders as spawned, i.e. as invisible blockers (DoesObjectCollideWithObjectAt consults only active, coordinates and elevation, never the invisible flag, so even MOVEMENT_TYPE_INVISIBLE would still block). Stubbed, not rewritten: no script interpreter runs this, and the maps that call it are a transcribed list rather than a parsed map-script table. Not modelled: the secret-base callers (data/scripts/shared_secret_base.inc:12-16) and flags 13/14's secret-base-only slots.

affine_tile_layer.reason: AffineTilemap/AffineBgLayer port SetBgAffine/SetBgAffineInternal-driven mode 1/2 affine BG semantics: 8bpp-only flat single-byte tile indices (no per-tile flip/palette bank), P/Q matrix (AffineMatrix, affine.rs) + 20.8 fixed-point reference-point texture-space sampling, and wrap (overflow=1) vs transparent (overflow=0) out-of-bounds handling, verified against mgba's GBAVideoSoftwareRendererDrawBackgroundMode2 and MODE_2_COORD_OVERFLOW/NO_OVERFLOW macros (software-bg.c). AffineBgLayer::sample_column_with_mosaic_hold adds the stateful transparent-overflow mosaic path: an off-map column is retried on the next column instead of blanking the rest of its block, an accepted column holds for the whole block (a palette-index-0 texel included), decoded horizontal block sizes 1 and 2 hold nothing, and a span reopening mid-block seeds its hold from the snapped block origin -- gated on the column before the span, yet fetched with wrapping rather than bounds-tested. The per-scanline sx/sy accumulation mgba's renderer performs collapses into one static per-frame closed-form sample under pokeemerald's observed once-per-frame BG2X/Y/PA..PD write pattern (bg.c:244-282); a game that rewrote the reference point mid-frame would observe different behavior, out of scope here. Slots into compose_frame via BgSlot::new_affine (issue #98, issue #872).

mosaic.reason: BgSlot::with_mosaic (compositor.rs) plus crate::mosaic::MosaicSize/MosaicConfig port BGxCNT's mosaic bit and the shared MOSAIC register's BG H/V block-size fields, verified against mgba's BACKGROUND_BITMAP_INIT mosaic macros (S-2 slice 4, issue #99). Stateless top-left snapping (coord - coord % size at composite time) covers regular 4bpp BGs and affine layers with wrap overflow, which additionally bypass horizontal snapping at decoded block sizes 1 and 2 (BgSlot::wrap_affine_bypasses_horizontal_mosaic). An affine layer with transparent overflow is not stateless: it runs the per-column AffineMosaicHold in bg_affine.rs, which retries past a rejected origin instead of blanking the block, holds the accepted texel for the rest of the block, holds nothing at decoded sizes 1 and 2, and seeds a mid-block reopened span from the snapped origin behind the preceding-column gate; compose_frame resets that hold at every surviving window span start on the scanline (issue #872). A regular 8bpp BG with horizontal size above 1 is per-span, not stateless: a window span starting mid-block holds the span-start pixel column of the scrolled start (BgLayer::sample_8bpp_mosaic_prefetch, selecting the tile by mGBA's (16 + offset) >> 3 rule) until the next block boundary, restarting at every pass start, verified against mgba's DRAW_BACKGROUND_MODE_0_MOSAIC_256 (software-mode0.c:320-408; issue #2026). Complements regular_tile_layer/affine_tile_layer/scroll_wrapping.

OBJ_EVENT_GFX_to_graphics_info.reason: npc::resolve_sprite_source (with npc/sheets.rs object_sheet and initial_berry_sheet) is a bounded re-derivation of this table's OBJ_EVENT_GFX_* -> gObjectEventGraphicsInfo_* mapping and of each pointed-to struct's .width/.height/.paletteTag/.paletteSlot/.inanimate/.images/.anims fields (object_event_graphics_info.h, object_event_pic_tables.h, object_event_anims.h) for every graphics id the fixed object events of the checkpoint maps name. Modelled: the two protagonist sheets and both rival variants (reusing the matching protagonist's art, kept on its own palette bank for PALSLOT_NPC_SPECIAL), 26 standard nine-frame 16x32 people, the 16x16 ninja boy, item ball, Birch's bag, cuttable tree, moving box and two dolls, the 16x32 nurse and mystery-event deliveryman (4- and 3-cell sheets), the two 32x32 Vigoroth variants and Zigzagoon, the 48x48 truck, and Route 103's three berry trees at the BERRY_STAGE_BERRIES stage new_game.inc plants them at (resolved per event by trainer_sight_or_berry_tree_id; no berry state, growth, planting or watering). Each graphic shows its stationary frame for the object's live facing: the cell sAnimTable_Standard/_Nurse/_Inanimate/_CuttableTree/_BerryTree select for that facing, with the pic table's own cell remapping (Vigoroth cells 0 and 3, nurse and deliveryman cells 0-2); walking, bowing, cutting and growth animation are not run. Packing keeps only the sheet cells some facing of some event of the scene can show (sheets::Facing::reachable_cells: south, north and west for a directional sheet, its one cell for a fixed one), so a live turn such as faceplayer always lands on a packed frame. The packed sheets are the scene's ROM-side image store, not OBJ VRAM: composing stages only each frame's drawn sprites into OBJ VRAM (obj_vram::stage), so the ten-bit OBJ tile field bounds one frame's sprites, not the scene's sheets. Upstream's single resident NPC_SPECIAL palette slot (the last special palette loaded wins) is not reproduced: moving box, truck, Vigoroth and Zigzagoon each get their own native bank. Not modelled: the OBJ_EVENT_GFX_VAR_1..VAR_B decoration slots and every non-rival OBJ_EVENT_GFX_VAR_0 value (GetObjectEventGraphicsInfo's VarGetObjectEventGraphicsId indirection, event_object_movement.c:1914-1931, is modelled for n == 0 narrowed to the two rival ids), every graphics id outside the checkpoint maps, and the rest of this 239-entry table's rows.

DoGroundEffects_OnBeginStep.reason: event_object_movement.c:8098-8116. OverworldPhase::step runs the player's begin-step pass for the tall-grass flag only, from the frame a step starts (StepOutcome::Advanced) and from the crossing step on the entered map (finish_crossing), after the step's own elevation update. Every object event's pass is OverworldScene::object_steps_began (crates/pokeemerald-rs/src/overworld/grass.rs), run by OverworldPhase::advance_object_events after the frame's scheduler callbacks: an admitted object whose live tile differs from the tile of its last ground-effect pass has begun a step (ObjectEventState::walk commits the destination when the step begins), and a step onto tall grass starts a rustling effect owned by that object, with the elevation CellElevations::settled gives its new tile. The scheduler moves no wanderer yet, so only a direct walk exercises it today. Every other begin-step ground effect (long grass, puddles, ripples, sand, ash, shadows) is unmodelled, as is a begin-step pass for a position change that is not a step.

DoGroundEffects_OnSpawn.reason: event_object_movement.c:8080-8096. Two halves of the spawn-frame ground-effect pass are modelled. Elevation (crates/pokeemerald-rs/src/overworld/sprites.rs): sprites::CellElevations::update stores on an object its own layout-grid cell's elevation (ObjectEventState::update_elevation, unless that cell is ELEVATION_TRANSITION, which keeps the retained one, or either it or the previous cell is ELEVATION_MULTI_LEVEL, or it lies off the grid; the ObjectEventUpdateElevation :7759-7771 pass DoGroundEffects_OnSpawn reaches on the spawn frame: :4931, gated by triggerGroundEffectsOnMove = TRUE from InitObjectEventStateFromTemplate :1301), so May's Pichu doll authored at elevation 4 on a cell of elevation 3 draws at priority 2; OverworldScene::update_object_elevations runs it for every live object when the collection is created and around each frame's scheduler callbacks, and SceneSprites::live_entries and the tall-grass effects read the stored ObjectEventState::previous_elevation. Tall grass (crates/pokeemerald-rs/src/overworld/grass.rs): OverworldScene::seed_tall_grass_placement is the player's spawn-time pass for the tall-grass flag only, once per placement (triggerGroundEffectsOnMove is true for a fresh object, :1301, and after a return to the field, :1799-1802: a battle return re-arms it). OverworldScene::seed_object_tall_grass is every other object event's pass for the same flag: OverworldPhase::advance_object_events runs it ahead of the frame's scheduler callbacks, as the pass opens UpdateObjectEventCurrentMovement (:4931), and again after the scheduler's map-load admission on a scene's first frame, so each object the scheduler has admitted (ObjectEventCollection, LiveObjectEvent::is_active) standing on tall grass gets a settled effect once, whether or not object events are frozen; a hidden, out-of-view, or removed object has none (an admitted entry whose hide flag has since been set counts as removed, since the scheduler does not retire it and RemoveObjectEventByLocalIdAndMap would have), and an object the scheduler re-admits is passed again, as its template reinitialisation sets triggerGroundEffectsOnMove (:1301). A return to the field re-arms every object (OverworldScene::reset_field_effects, ResetObjectEventFldEffData :1795-1806). Stubbed: every other spawn-time ground effect (long grass, ripples, sand, puddles, shadows, reflections) is unmodelled; UpdateObjectEventElevationAndPriority is separately tracked. engine::overworld::warp_destination_position (crates/engine/src/overworld/warp.rs) is this port's model of that same spawn-frame resolution for OverworldPhase::warp_to's resolved-warp landings.

DoesObjectCollideWithObjectAt.reason: COLLISION_OBJECT_EVENT: the occupancy test (:4724-4741), re-implemented as object_event_collision::Occupant::holds. An object holds its current tile and its previous tile, so a walker blocks the tile it is leaving until ObjectEventState::settle_previous_position shifts previous onto current, and AreElevationsCompatible's either-side-ELEVATION_TRANSITION wildcard decides elevation. Two consumers: an object's own step (collision_in_direction, ObjectEventCollection::collision_in_direction, which scans every other admitted entry and the player's current and previous tiles from FrameContext) and the player's landing and a trainer's sight line: PlayerState::step's COLLISION_OBJECT_EVENT check goes through engine::overworld::object_event::blocking_object_event_at over MapRuntime::collision_objects_at, and trainer_sight's intermediate-tile check scans ObjectEventCollection::collision_objects_at directly. The identification query GetObjectEventIdByPosition stays current-tile only. Narrowed: the player's own step has no self-skip because the player is a PlayerState, never a collection entry; the collection-bound query scans admitted entries only, as upstream's active check does (:4730-4733), so an unadmitted or despawned entry holds no tile. The hide flag is not read on that bound scan: the scheduler applied it at admission, so an object whose flag is set after admission keeps blocking until a script retires it. blocking_object_event_at filters by the hide flag only for an unbound runtime, which scans authored templates; a connection landing runs the same test after terrain, directional impassability and elevation: PlayerState asks ConnectedMapData::carried_object_event_blocks, which the phase's MapConnections answers by running ObjectEventCollection::collision_objects_at over the live objects ObjectEventCollection::carry_across_connection would keep, in the entered map's coordinates. The entered map's fresh templates are not scanned, since none has spawned and upstream scans only active objects.

Narrowed: a tile off the decoded grid is impassable rather than looked up in a connected map's backup band (GetMapBorderIdAt, fieldmap.c:522-557); the camera-tracked CanCameraMoveInDirection term is the player's and not modelled. No movement type calls it yet.

GetObjectEventIdByPosition.reason: Position-plus-elevation-wildcard object-event identification rewritten as MapRuntime::object_events_at, which matches each object's current tile alone: upstream's scan compares currentCoords only (:2192-2215), so a walker is found on the tile it has entered, not the one it is leaving; MapRuntime::collision_objects_at is the collision counterpart. With a bound ObjectEventCollection (MapRuntime::with_object_events) it delegates to ObjectEventCollection::object_events_at and compares each object's live position and elevation, returning the authored template as metadata; a bound collection never falls back to authored coordinates. Unbound runtimes still scan authored coordinates. ObjectEventDoesElevationMatch's rule (either side's ELEVATION_TRANSITION is a wildcard) is the shared collision::elevations_compatible predicate. It returns an iterator over every match on the tile, not a single hit, and scans only the entries the scheduler has admitted: ObjectEventCollection::object_events_at skips an entry whose Lifecycle is not active, the counterpart of upstream's `gObjectEvents[i].active` guard (:2198-2200), so an unadmitted or retired entry is invisible to the query. The template hide flag is not read at query time: the scheduler applied it at admission, so a flag cleared while the camera is still admits nothing until the next camera update, and a flag set after admission leaves the entry in the scan until a script retires it. engine::overworld::object_event::visible_object_event_at therefore filters by the hide flag only for an unbound runtime, which scans authored coordinates (sight, rendering and tests that bind no collection). The facing lookup (facing_object_event) and interaction go through that composed search; PlayerState::step's COLLISION_OBJECT_EVENT check goes through its collision counterpart, engine::overworld::object_event::blocking_object_event_at, which applies the same bound-or-unbound hide-flag rule. Templates stack per tile with independent flags (the Birch lab's three starter balls at (6, 8)). Known narrowing: live elevation is the state's currentElevation, which OverworldScene::update_object_elevations updates from the ground as ObjectEventUpdateElevation does (event_object_movement.c:7759-7771; see that row); cross-map objects are not migrated. Callers must run the map-load admission pass (ObjectEventCollection::admit_on_map_load or the first run_frame) before querying a freshly seeded collection.

Priority is read on every compose from each object's stored retained elevation (OverworldScene::compose_live).

UpdateWalkSlowAnim.reason: WALK_SLOW_FRAMES_PER_TILE and TransitCadence::WALK_SLOW: the slow walk moves a pixel every other update until 16 pixels are taken, so one tile takes 31 updates (event_object_movement.c:8318-8342); its walk animation runs the four 8-frame sAnim_Go* cells, rendered by crates/pokeemerald-rs/src/overworld/avatar/mat.rs. Used by the spin mat's exit step (MovementAction_WalkSlow*, :5140-5155, 5226-5290); the NPC walk-slow movement actions are not ported. The camera follows the same displacement: crates/pokeemerald-rs/src/overworld/viewport.rs's camera_lag_px covers ceil(k / 2) pixels after k updates for this step.

gDirectionBlockedMetatileFuncs.reason: See gOppositeDirectionBlockedMetatileFuncs: same fold into collision::directionally_impassable. This table pairs each direction with the OPPOSITE predicate (north -> IsSouthBlocked, west -> IsEastBlocked, ...) and is applied to MapGridGetMetatileBehaviorAt(x, y), the destination tile (:4718).

gInitialMovementTypeFacingDirections.reason: Transcribed in full: engine::overworld::initial_facing_direction covers all 81 MOVEMENT_TYPE_* entries, mirroring InitObjectEventStateFromTemplate's initial-spawn-facing table. The scheduler (object_event_scheduler.rs) seeds and respawns the four fixed-facing types at that facing and then never re-derives it, since the face action re-faces the current direction, so a facing a script set persists until the object respawns. A MOVEMENT_TYPE_LOOK_AROUND or MOVEMENT_TYPE_FACE_DOWN_AND_RIGHT object starts at that facing and then turns on its own through the random-facing callbacks; a WANDER_*/WALK_* object still renders at its initial facing forever, since its own walking is not modelled yet.

gOppositeDirectionBlockedMetatileFuncs.reason: The direction-to-predicate pairing is folded into collision::directionally_impassable's match rather than transcribed as a function-pointer array (no-verbatim; Rust has no DIR_* index to key on -- Direction is an enum). This table pairs each direction with its own predicate and is applied to objectEvent->currentMetatileBehavior, the tile the mover stands on (:4717); its sibling gDirectionBlockedMetatileFuncs supplies the opposite pairing for the destination. Both pairings are pinned by their own tests in collision.rs, since swapping them is the failure mode this table's name invites.

gPlayerRunMovementActions.reason: The four-direction run action table collapses to TransitCadence::RUN at the crossing's chosen direction (event_object_movement.c:968-974).

sStepTimes.reason: Only the normal-speed entry is modelled: object_event_motion::NORMAL_STEP_FRAMES, the 16 frames of a normal walk counting the frame that starts the action, and StepAction::pixel_offset's one-pixel-a-frame closing of the committed tile. A normal walk in place lasts the same 16 frames by InitMoveInPlace's own duration (:5704-5759), not by this table. The slow, fast, faster, and jump-speed entries are not modelled.

CameraUpdate.reason: Per-frame gFieldCamera pixel-offset accumulator (movementSpeedX/Y ramping gTotalCameraPixelOffsetX/Y by 1px/frame toward a full metatile) collapsed to the analytic viewport::camera_lag_px, which derives the same net signed pixel lag as a closed form rather than replicating the accumulator: covered_px = step_progress * METATILE_PX / transit_duration, lag = METATILE_PX - covered_px. A tile is always METATILE_PX (16px) wide regardless of the active crossing's own frame count, so this scales correctly whether the crossing is an ordinary step, a dispatched MB_WALK_* tile (WALK_FRAMES_PER_TILE, one pixel per frame) or a dispatched MB_SLIDE_* tile (SLIDE_FRAMES_PER_TILE, two pixels per frame). It is a strictly bigger collapse than SetSpritePosToMapCoords' own entry: that one folds a compile-time constant (the player's own mapX - gSaveBlock1Ptr->pos.x is identically 0), while this folds a per-frame accumulator into a closed form, and only up to the constant term already folded into PLAYER_OBJ_X/Y, so it equals upstream's value on frame-to-frame differences rather than absolutely (see camera_lag_px's docs). Sharing one value keeps the BG scroll in build_tilemaps and the NPC placement in npc::oam_entries in lockstep, so a stationary NPC never snaps to its destination tile at step start while the BG still lags smoothly behind. UpdateObjectEventsForCameraUpdate's own spawn/despawn side effect (TrySpawnObjectEvents/RemoveObjectEventsOutsideView at camera tile boundaries) stays under its own event_object_movement.c ledger entries and is not claimed here.

DrawMetatile.reason: Per-METATILE_LAYER_TYPE bottom/middle/top BG-layer routing of a metatile's 8 raw tile entries, implemented in viewport::route_layers; NORMAL reproduces DrawMetatile's fixed 0x3014 write to all four BG3 cells.

DrawMetatileAt.reason: Per-position metatile-id lookup plus primary/secondary tileset dispatch (NUM_METATILES_IN_PRIMARY threshold) feeding DrawMetatile, ported into viewport::metatile_layers/cell_at.

FieldUpdateBgTilemapScroll.reason: BGnVOFS = sVerticalCameraPan + yPixelOffset + 8: the constant +8 term (issue #977) is now modeled as RESTING_SCROLL_Y, an unconditional 8px baseline build_tilemaps always adds to scroll_y, never just during a mid-step pan. yPixelOffset's own per-frame contribution is camera_lag_px (see CameraUpdate/UpdateCameraPanning's own entries); sHorizontalCameraPan/sVerticalCameraPan's dynamic bike pan-ahead is not modelled (no bike in this port yet) -- deferred, still in v1 scope.

InstallCameraPanAheadCallback.reason: Installed for every ordinary field (overworld.c:2139), this sets the resting sHorizontalCameraPan/sVerticalCameraPan to 0/32. The horizontal 0 needs no representation; the vertical 32 (issue #977) is folded into PLAYER_VIEW_ROW's crop, which anchors two metatile rows short of upstream's own MAP_OFFSET-based anchor, absorbing exactly that 32px. CameraPanningCB_PanAhead's own per-frame bike-speed adjustment to sVerticalCameraPan is not modelled (no bike in this port yet) -- deferred, still in v1 scope.

UpdateCameraPanning.reason: gSpriteCoordOffsetX/Y's per-frame derivation from the camera's own pixel state, ported as the shared viewport::camera_lag_px this port's two camera-driven consumers both read (issue #217, I-3): build_tilemaps subtracts it from the BG scroll (mirroring gSpriteCoordOffsetX/Y being the camera-locked complement to the world-locked BG scroll) and npc::oam_entries adds it to every stationary NPC's placement (mirroring UpdateOamCoords -- see src/sprite.c#UpdateOamCoords). The resting -sVerticalCameraPan - 8 bias this function folds into gSpriteCoordOffsetY (issue #977) is now modelled too: PLAYER_VIEW_ROW's crop absorbs the -32, and avatar::PLAYER_OBJ_Y subtracts RESTING_SCROLL_Y for the remaining -8, so the fixed player/NPC OAM origin sits at the same screen row upstream's resting gSpriteCoordOffsetY produces. sHorizontalCameraPan/sVerticalCameraPan's dynamic bike pan-ahead term is not modelled yet (no bike in this port yet) -- deferred, still in v1 scope.

CheckStandardWildEncounter.reason: field_control_avatar.c:116-122,162-163,668-686. Immunity, reset, and remembered behavior are implemented by WildEncounterState; OverworldPhase observes completed positional steps and stationary turns on the callback after animation drain. Forced tile centres and earlier coord/step-door events suppress the check; successful encounters preempt arrow, interaction, animated-door, START, and movement handling.

ClearPoisonStepCounter.reason: field_control_avatar.c:632-635. OverworldPhase::clear_poison_step_counter zeroes VAR_POISON_STEP_COUNTER (0x402B, constants/vars.h:61) and runs as each modelled battle (wild, first, Route 103 rival, sight trainer) starts, at the common active-battle dispatch boundary, matching battle_setup.c:365-372,930-943. The upstream trainer-battle call sites outside those modelled battles are not part of this entry.

FieldGetPlayerInput.reason: Partially modeled by phase-owned field-input gates. Completed keypad positional steps feed tookStep consumers, except the escalator arrival's walk-off: that east step is held movement (field_player_avatar.c:353-379), so runningState stays NOT_MOVING and tookStep is never set (field_control_avatar.c:118-119); OverworldPhase::take_stepped_onto (flow/overworld_phase/escalator_arrival.rs) withholds its landing from those consumers and leaves it to the encounter gate (:120-121). Completed stationary turns additionally feed checkStandardWildEncounter without positional coord/warp work, after timer drain and subject to forced-tile exclusion (field_control_avatar.c:116-122). Existing tile-center/at-rest button gating remains. Deferred in v1: PLAYER_SPEED_FASTEST screening, pressedSelectButton, pressedBButton, heldDirection2 separate TryDoorWarp read, and dpadDirection outside-gate handling. tookStep also increments GAME_STAT_STEPS: OverworldPhase::step calls GameStats::increment(GameStat::Steps) through OverworldPhase::count_took_step on the completed, non-forced landing (the stepped_onto fact from OverworldPhase::take_stepped_onto, which already drops a forced landing through field_input_suppressed and withholds the escalator arrival's held walk-off) right after take_stepped_onto and before first_battle_trigger_ready, so a landing that then starts a coord event, door warp, step script or encounter still counts (field_control_avatar.c:89-122,155-163; overworld.c:433-445).

GetBackgroundEventAtPosition.reason: Ordered background-event lookup with event-zero-or-equal elevation matching.

GetInFrontOfPlayerPosition.reason: The facing-tile position (GetXYCoordsOneStepInFrontOfPlayer, player position + facing delta) plus the elevation rule rewritten as the engine-internal front_tile, shared by facing_object_event and select_interaction_target: the player's own grid cell only selects the wildcard (ELEVATION_TRANSITION cell or off-grid), otherwise the query is the retained previousElevation that PlayerGetElevation returns, not the collision elevation.

GetInteractedBackgroundEventScript.reason: Typed sign and hidden-item selection with collected flags; north-facing secret-base entrance context only, saved-base eligibility and special-variable setup remain deferred.

GetInteractedMetatileScript.script_targe.reason: Classifies all 24 script-returning metatile branches into 23 typed targets, preserving north-facing gates and exact secret-base elevation equality. Furniture and poster save bookkeeping, script launch, services, water-move gating, and cross-kind precedence remain outside this sub-artifact.

GetInteractedObjectEventScript.reason: Selects the visible live object at the front tile, else, only when the front tile is a counter, the one on its far side at the same query elevation (field_control_avatar.c:287-313); an object whose script is null selects nothing and falls through without the counter retry. The result carries the object's local id (gSpecialVar_LastTalked) and the player's facing (gSpecialVar_Facing). Not modelled: writing gSelectedObjectEvent and the special variables, the Trainer Hill script override, and the saved RAM-script override GetRamScript applies.

GetInteractionScript.reason: engine::overworld::select_interaction_target selects the first target of GetInteractedObjectEventScript, GetInteractedBackgroundEventScript, then GetInteractedMetatileScript (script-returning branches only) as a typed InteractionTarget, querying the tile in front of the player at the elevation GetInFrontOfPlayerPosition derives and reading that front tile's metatile behavior (field_control_avatar.c:170-172,240-258). A secret-base entrance already among the caller's saved secret bases selects no background event, so the metatile stage runs next (TrySetCurSecretBase failing, field_control_avatar.c:354-361). Not selected: GetInteractedWaterScript (Surf and Waterfall), because water eligibility depends on party and badge state; launching the selected script, which stays with the caller.

IsArrowWarpMetatileBehavior.reason: engine::overworld::warp::is_arrow_warp_trigger: dispatches by direction to metatile_behavior::is_{north,south,west,east}_arrow_warp exactly as upstream's sArrowWarpMetatileBehaviorChecks table does (field_player_avatar.c:226-232). Issue #174.

RestartWildEncounterImmunitySteps.reason: field_control_avatar.c:662-666. Fully modelled as WildEncounterState::restart_immunity_steps -- zeroes the step counter only, deliberately leaving sPrevMetatileBehavior alone as upstream does (they are two separate statics). Wired at this port's counterparts of upstream's map-load call sites: OverworldPhase::warp_to (LoadMapFromWarp, overworld.c:850) and OverworldPhase::cross_connection (LoadMapFromCameraTransition, overworld.c:800 -- the piece issue #177 explicitly deferred to this slice). The battle-start call sites (battle_setup.c:370, :941) are covered by CheckStandardWildEncounter's own reset on a fired encounter, which upstream also performs (:679).

TryArrowWarp.reason: GetWarpEventAtMapPosition + IsArrowWarpMetatileBehavior + SetupWarp/DoWarp's warp-resolution shape absorbed into engine::overworld::warp::trigger_arrow_warp, a separate entry point from the door-shaped trigger_door_warp precisely because the two are gated differently upstream. Called from crates/pokeemerald-rs/src/flow/overworld_phase/step.rs's OverworldPhase::step as a per-frame poll, upstream's own gating: the direction currently held must equal the direction the player currently faces (input->heldDirection && input->dpadDirection == playerDirection, field_control_avatar.c:164-168), evaluated at the tile the player is standing on, independent of tookStep -- so it fires both for a step taken onto an arrow tile while still holding its direction and for a turn in place while already standing on one. The only added gate is that the player be at rest between steps, which is this port's counterpart to the T_TILE_CENTER/T_NOT_MOVING test that sets heldDirection upstream in the first place (:95-112). Issue #174 (the Brendan's-house exit doormat, MAP_LITTLEROOT_TOWN_BRENDANS_HOUSE_1F warp #1 at (8, 8)). Issue #194 corrected the frame ordering against ProcessPlayerFieldInput (overworld.c:1444-1455), which runs this check *before* PlayerStep and skips the step outright when it fires: OverworldPhase::step evaluates this gate ahead of its own movement call and, when it already fires, skips movement for the frame entirely instead of running it and polling afterward -- so a legal, walkable step in the arrow direction warps rather than stepping (previously a permanent no-warp, unreachable on bundled data since every arrow tile's own direction is impassable there, and pinned now by a synthetic scene in flow/overworld_phase/warp_tests/arrow.rs). Issue #1039 then corrected which frame that single pre-movement poll belongs to. There is now no post-movement poll at all: OverworldPhase::step holds a landing whose walk animation just drained until the *next* call and processes it there, ahead of the arrow poll, because upstream's T_TILE_CENTER needs PlayerCheckIfAnimFinishedOrInactive (field_player_avatar.c:901-915) to see a heldMovementFinished that only the previous frame's CB2 AnimateSprites could have set (main.c:188-195, overworld.c:1438-1469). So a 16-frame tile crossing is polled on call 17, not on call 16: holding the arrow direction through call 16 and releasing it on call 17 does not warp, and the door-shaped trigger_door_warp for that same landing is resolved on call 17 too, above this poll, in ProcessPlayerFieldInput's own order (TryStartStepBasedScript :155-161, CheckStandardWildEncounter :162, then TryArrowWarp :164-168). Pinned by the frame-17 stair-warp regression in flow/overworld_phase/warp_tests/ordinary.rs and the doormat regressions in flow/overworld_phase/warp_tests/arrow.rs. Not modelled: StoreInitialPlayerAvatarState's pre-warp avatar snapshot, and SetupWarp's escape-warp/Trainer Hill bookkeeping.

TryDoorWarp.reason: GetInFrontOfPlayerPosition + MetatileBehavior_IsWarpDoor + GetWarpEventAtMapPosition's animated-door gate absorbed into engine::overworld::warp::trigger_animated_door_warp, a new entry point distinct from the completed-step trigger_door_warp. The flow-side decision (facing tile + that gate) is owned by crates/pokeemerald-rs/src/flow/overworld_phase/animated_door.rs; OverworldPhase::step only sequences its outcome, pre-movement only (the at-rest preempt, gated on input->heldDirection2 && input->dpadDirection == playerDirection, field_control_avatar.c:175-178, the same held-direction value already computed for the arrow-warp poll). There is no post-movement poll; crates/pokeemerald-rs/src/flow/overworld_phase/animated_door.rs owns the timing derivation. The check additionally requires direction == DIR_NORTH (:833-841). Issue #851: a real animated-door tile is always solid, so trigger_door_warp's own completed-step poll (issue #174's TryStartWarpEventScript path) can never reach one -- PlayerState::try_start_resolved_step rejects any nonzero-collision landing before it can exist. Pinned by real Littleroot Town regressions (the Professor Birch's-lab front door, both a stationary approach and a walked one) in flow/overworld_phase/warp_tests/door.rs, by animated_door.rs's own decision tests, and by door_sequencing_tests.rs's drain-call sequencing ratchet (a pack-free whole-frame test cannot observe that one: a failed warp_to preserves map_id and position). Not modelled: TryDoorWarp's secret-base branch, and DoDoorWarp's opening-animation sequence (the warp still resolves immediately, matching every other warp path in this port). Issue #1039 left the pre-movement placement itself untouched but gave it the same frame boundary as every other field-input check: the completed step that the previous call's animation drained is processed at the start of this call, above it, so a coord event, a door-shaped warp or a wild encounter on that landing returns from ProcessPlayerFieldInput (:155-162) before this check at :170-178 runs. A walked approach's door therefore still opens on the call after the approach's animation drains -- upstream's first T_TILE_CENTER CB1 for that crossing -- which is the timing animated_door.rs already derived.

TryStartInteractionScript.reason: OverworldPhase::step's A-press handling routes the target engine::overworld::select_interaction_target selects (object, then background event, then script-backed metatile; GetInteractionScript's order). An object script crate::overworld::npc_scripts::script_text recognizes opens a NpcDialog from that module's own small hardcoded msgbox-style table, and the Route 103 rival object starts its battle. Every other selected target (an unrecognized object script, a sign, hidden item or secret-base entrance, a script-backed metatile) consumes the frame as InteractionOutcome::Unmodelled, matching TryStartInteractionScript returning TRUE for any non-NULL script (field_control_avatar.c:172), but starts no script. A secret-base entrance is selected only when the list of saved secret bases passed to the selector lacks its base, as TrySetCurSecretBase requires (field_control_avatar.c:354-361); the save block holds no secret bases, so this application passes an empty list and every north-facing entrance is selected. Reading the saved bases from the save is not modelled. Only a press that selects nothing lets the frame's direction input reach PlayerState unconsumed. Not modelled: GetInteractedWaterScript, GetInteractedLinkPlayerScript, RamScript, and the interaction sound effect (PlaySE(SE_SELECT)). The lookup runs from the frame-start (pre-movement) player position and facing, before PlayerStep could turn or step the player, matching ProcessPlayerFieldInput reading playerDirection/position before ever calling PlayerStep (field_control_avatar.c:143-145, overworld.c:1444-1455). It sits below the completed step's own events, as upstream does: a landing whose walk animation drained is processed at the start of the next step call (upstream's T_TILE_CENTER CB1, field_player_avatar.c:901-915 over main.c:188-195 / overworld.c:1438-1469), and a coord event, a door-shaped warp or a wild encounter claiming that landing (TryStartStepBasedScript :155-161, CheckStandardWildEncounter :162) returns from ProcessPlayerFieldInput before this check at :172 is ever reached, so the A press is not consumed on that frame.

TryStartWarpEventScript.reason: The completed-step door and escalator branches (field_control_avatar.c:702-714, with IsWarpMetatileBehavior :753-765). engine::overworld::warp::trigger_door_warp and trigger_escalator_warp resolve GetWarpEventAtMapPosition on the arrived tile, with no direction gate; OverworldPhase::step (crates/pokeemerald-rs/src/flow/overworld_phase/step.rs) polls both at the retained previous elevation as one completed-step warp, ahead of the wild-encounter roll and the arrow poll. Pinned for both Oldale Pokemon Center escalators (1F warp 2 to 2F warp 0, and back) by the checkpoint regressions in flow/overworld_phase/warp_tests/checkpoint.rs. Not modelled: StoreInitialPlayerAvatarState, SetupWarp's escape-warp bookkeeping, and the ladder, Lavaridge, Aqua Hideout, Union Room, Mt. Pyre and Mossdeep branches (:715-745), whose behaviors is_warp_trigger does not accept.

UpdatePoisonStepCounter.reason: field_control_avatar.c:637-659. OverworldPhase::update_poison_step_counter advances VAR_POISON_STEP_COUNTER (a saved event var, so Save and Continue keep the cycle) modulo four with u16 wraparound on each completed step outside a Secret Base and the Union Room, runs DoPoisonFieldEffect on the wrap, and claims the frame only for a faint (FLDPSN_FNT), so an ordinary poison tick leaves the wild-encounter roll, arrow warp, and interaction to the same frame. It sits after the coord event and door warp and before the encounter roll, and is skipped on forced-movement tiles (field_control_avatar.c:155-163,543-553). Not modelled: EventScript_FieldPoison itself (data/scripts/field_poison.inc:1-17) -- the port routes the faint through a typed phase call because the TryFieldPoisonWhiteOut special has no script callback -- and the other TryStartStepCountScript step counters (rematch, friendship, Faraway Island, egg hatch, abnormal weather).

FieldCallback_EscalatorWarpIn.reason: Partly modelled (field_effect.c:1690-1702, Task_EscalatorWarpIn :1707-1722,1800-1818). OverworldPhase::begin_escalator_arrival faces the player east and the next field frame's input becomes one east step (EscalatorWarpIn_Init's face-east hold and EscalatorWarpIn_End's GetWalkNormalMovementAction(DIR_EAST)), so an escalator-triggered warp ends one tile east of the destination warp tile, facing east; the walk goes through PlayerState::step, so collision takes the normal path. That step is held movement, not keypad movement (field_player_avatar.c:353-379), so runningState stays NOT_MOVING and FieldGetPlayerInput sets no tookStep (field_control_avatar.c:118-119): OverworldPhase::step withholds its landing from the took-step consumers (coord event, completed-step warp, step-count script and its poison counter, :155-161) and keeps the encounter-gate observation, which needs only T_TILE_CENTER (:120-121). OverworldPhase::step starts it only after a completed-step escalator warp lands. Not modelled: the arrival fade (WarpFadeInScreen), Overworld_PlaySpecialMapMusic, the field-control lock and camera freeze while the escalator settles, and StopEscalator's tile animation (fldeff_escalator.c).  runningState staying NOT_MOVING also makes a held direction other than east turn before it steps (field_player_avatar.c:587-595): the walk-off's landing ends the keypad's moving streak.

FldEff_TallGrass.reason: field_effect_helpers.c:291-314. TallGrassEffects::push creates the effect on its tile with the owner's previous elevation and OBJ priority 2, drawn as a 16x16 OBJ whose top-left sits one metatile below an object event's 16x32 top (SetSpritePosToOffsetMapCoords(+8, +8), centre to corner), palette bank 6; the settled variant seeks to command 4. The effect carries its owner (grass::Owner): the player, or the object event's slot in the scene's live ObjectEventCollection, standing for sLocalId/sMapNum/sMapGroup (:305-307), since a scene holds one map.

UpdateGrassFieldEffectSubpriority.reason: field_effect_helpers.c:1662-1690. TallGrassEffect::subpriority is SetObjectSubpriorityByElevation (npc::subpriority_from_bottom) plus the overlap rule against the player's and every bound object-event sprite's depth, with upstream's strict bounds and first-match break. Not modelled: object events whose graphics the scene does not bind (they draw no sprite here); an object whose graphic is not 16x32 is compared with 16x32 bounds from its parent's top-left rather than with its own centre and height.

UpdateTallGrassFieldEffect.reason: field_effect_helpers.c:316-355. TallGrassEffects::advance runs the callback ahead of the animation step as AnimateSprites does (sprite.c:308-320): remove when the tile is no longer MB_TALL_GRASS, or once the owner's current and previous tiles both left it (each effect against its own Owner's tiles) or the owner cannot be found, as TryGetObjectEventIdByLocalIdAndMap fails for a removed object (:332-337) and the animation had already ended; the first-command subpriority bias; on-screen culling as UpdateObjectEventSpriteInvisibility. A connection crossing (:325-330) carries the live effects of the player and of every object the crossing keeps into the entered scene (OverworldScene::carry_tall_grass_from): the tile is translated by the crossing's departed-to-entered offset, and animation, moved-away, elevation and depth state are kept, so the effect ends by the callback's own three conditions rather than at the scene swap. The departed tile's behaviour is read from the departed scene as the effect crosses and kept with it (the entered scene holds no attributes for its connected layouts), and an effect whose translated tile lies outside the entered map's backup band (viewport::within_backup_map_band) is dropped. An object-owned effect is keyed by its owner's LiveObjectEvent::id and is dropped with an owner the crossing did not keep; the owner's ground-effect pass crosses with it, so the entered scene runs no second spawn-time pass. Not modelled: the camera saved-view cells upstream also copies into the entered map's backup grid (fieldmap.c:473,617).

CheckForPlayerAvatarCollision.reason: Destination-tile collision check re-implemented via MapRuntime::metatile_cell plus collision.rs's Collision, elevation_mismatch, and directionally_impassable, and (issue #161, I-3 lane) the object-event occupancy test -- the grid collision-bit, directional-impassability, elevation-mismatch and object-event cases, applied in GetCollisionAtCoords' own order (shared between the same-map and connection-crossing step paths via PlayerState::try_start_resolved_step, issue #440). PlayerStep.reason: Per-input-poll orchestration, on-foot only (the bike branch and every special-anim interrupt other than the slow-walk bump below are not ported), re-implemented as PlayerState::step. The WALK_IN_PLACE_FAST turn-in-place case of TryInterruptObjectEventSpecialAnim's non-interruptible window is modeled by the eight-frame turn_frames_remaining busy timer, so ordinary movement input stays gated for the turn's duration unless a dialog or the start menu takes the field lock first, in which case PlayerState::clear_turn_lock ends the window immediately, matching upstream's PlayerFreeze (field_player_avatar.c:1039-1046, event_object_lock.c's Task_FreezePlayer). Forced-movement classification is modeled via is_forced_movement, and the standing tile's dispatch runs before the keypad is read at all, even on a None poll, matching TryDoMetatileBehaviorForcedMovement's placement ahead of MovePlayerAvatarUsingKeypadInput (field_player_avatar.c:332-349): a supported tile commits its direction through resolve_landing/try_start_resolved_step, exactly as DoForcedMovement calls moveFunc on a clear route (:407-470): MB_WALK_* at PlayerWalkNormal's 16 frames per tile (:486-503), MB_SLIDE_* at PlayerWalkFast's 8 with facing locked (:526-552), ice and the Trick House puzzle floor via ForcedMovement_Slip along movementDirection at 8 frames with the animation paused but facing not locked (:473-484), and the four currents via PlayerRideWaterCurrent in their fixed directions at 6 frames with the animation running (:506-524, 985-988; event_object_movement.c:8263-8270). A finished slide crossing keeps its paused forward-foot pose (PlayerState::slide_pose_held) until the next keypad poll, field lock (PlayerFreeze, :1039-1046), or scripted facing, because ForcedMovement_Slide's disableAnim leaves the sprite animation paused until ForcedMovement_None's enableAnim and the standing face-direction action restart it (:429-440, 525-531, 588-600, event_object_movement.c:7302-7313). Every other armed behavior (the waterfall and the muddy slope, whose ForcedMovement_* physics are not ported) refuses every manual poll, including a would-be turn, except when its own forced direction is itself collision-blocked, in which case (matching TryDoMetatileBehaviorForcedMovement returning FALSE and PlayerStep falling through to MovePlayerAvatarUsingKeypadInput, :342-349) the poll is honoured as an ordinary manual step via the forced_movement_direction/forced_direction_blocked helpers; the two Secret Base mats are dispatched ahead of this fallback instead (PlayerState::forced_mat, crates/engine/src/overworld/player/mat.rs), since ForcedMovement_MatJump and ForcedMovement_MatSpin never collision-check and return TRUE (:555-565). A supported tile's own blocked forced route leaves the guard armed instead of clearing it: GetForcedMovementByMetatileBehavior re-reads the standing tile's behavior fresh every poll rather than latching a one-time verdict (:409-426), so only a successful dispatch or the player actually leaving the tile clears the guard, and a later poll retries the same dispatch once whatever blocked it (a wall, an object event) no longer does. The keypad still runs on the very poll a blocked attempt was found on (:344-348), and dispatch_forced_mover leaves the movement streak untouched on that blocked attempt, matching DoForcedMovement's collision branch leaving runningState alone (:443-462), so the retry still turns in place first rather than stepping immediately. The guard only arms from a manual MOVING attempt this PlayerState itself made (set in step before collision resolves, from the standing tile's behavior when it has a dispatched handler or is a Secret Base mat, so a blocked bump still arms a dispatched tile (a mat included) but never traps a deferred behavior, matching upstream selecting MOVING before collision at field_player_avatar.c:583-595; a successful landing then re-arms from the landing tile's own behavior in try_start_resolved_step): a warp arrival or a resumed save that places the avatar onto a forced-movement tile via PlayerState::new starts controllable, since arming on a placement would trap an unsupported behavior with no keypad fallback at all. OverworldPhase::step in crates/pokeemerald-rs/src/flow/overworld_phase/step.rs suppresses the arrow-warp poll, the animated-door check, the same-frame NPC interaction, and start_menu.rs's OverworldPhase::start_menu_may_open (its sixth gate) on a forced landing's tile-center frame alone, through PlayerState::field_input_suppressed: FieldGetPlayerInput's gate is (T_TILE_CENTER && !forcedMove) || T_NOT_MOVING, so forcedMove, computed from the wider MetatileBehavior_IsForcedMovementTile set rather than the dispatch table, closes only the first arm, and a player at rest on a forced tile still reaches TryArrowWarp/TryStartInteractionScript/TryDoorWarp/pressedStartButton (field_control_avatar.c:93-113). A collision-blocked manual step starts a 32-frame slow in-place walk (BUMP_IN_PLACE_FRAMES, PlayerNotOnBikeCollide's WalkInPlaceSlow, field_player_avatar.c:1011-1015, event_object_movement.c:5713-5735) that PlayerState::step consults before forced dispatch and the keypad, as TryInterruptObjectEventSpecialAnim does (field_player_avatar.c:332-382): a neutral poll or a repeat of the still-blocked direction is swallowed as Idle, and any other poll cancels the bump and is processed normally, so a changed direction steps at once instead of turning. A dialog or menu field lock, a scripted face, or a successful step cancels it too.

CopyPartyAndObjectsToSave.reason: CopyPartyAndObjectsToSave/FromSave (:196-206) and the SavePlayerParty/LoadPlayerParty pair they wrap (:160-178) are OverworldPhase::copy_party_and_objects_to_save (the player object event, then the lead flush) and the lead-owner load OverworldPhase::load_lead_from_save (crates/pokeemerald-rs/src/flow/overworld_phase/lead_owner.rs), with the flush OverworldPhase::flush_lead_to_save in the same file, called around every start-menu save and on every continue; the party half of both lives in lead_owner.rs, and OverworldPhase::copy_party_and_objects_to_save in crates/pokeemerald-rs/src/flow/overworld_phase/start_menu.rs keeps the player object-event write and delegates the party write to the flush. gPlayerParty is this port's single party::LoadedLead (battler, backing record, slot), encoded to and from SaveBlock1::playerParty[party::LoadedLead::slot] -- the continue-selected slot, not a fixed index 0 -- by pokeemerald_rs::party -- species, level, accumulated experience (MON_DATA_EXP, real state rather than a function of the level), personality/nature, the six IVs, the moveset with per-slot PP, the packed ppBonuses byte (written back byte-exact, including bits for slots the moveset does not fill, so a load/save cycle cannot strip a save's PP Ups; pinned by pp_ups_survive_the_round_trip_byte_for_byte and pp_bonus_bits_for_unknown_slots_are_not_stripped in crates/pokeemerald-rs/src/party/tests/codec.rs), current HP, the ability slot and the OT id all round-trip, so a continued session fights the mon that was saved. Upstream's copy is a whole-struct assignment; the save half here is party::merge_into_save_pokemon, which overlays only those battle-authoritative fields onto the record the slot was loaded from -- the six EVs among them, written from the battler's own (possibly KO-incremented) values -- so everything battle::BattlePokemon does not model -- contest condition, accumulated friendship, pokerus, met location/level/game, poke ball, OT gender, ribbons, nickname, OT name, language, markings, mail, the egg bit and non-volatile status -- is retained as the save's own bytes rather than rewritten. The held item is the exception: the merge files battle::BattlePokemon::held_item into the growth substructure, so a take (party::take_held_item, S-6) reaches the save and a Berry consumed in battle (Cmd_removeitem's ITEM_NONE, battle_script_commands.c:5901-:5909) stays consumed across SAVE and Continue, as the whole-struct copy persists it upstream (pinned by a_berry_consumed_in_battle_stays_consumed_after_save_and_reload in crates/pokeemerald-rs/src/party/tests/consumed_berry.rs). party::to_save_pokemon writes CreateMon's own default for whichever of those it can derive from its own two arguments: nickname (the species' display name), language (GAME_LANGUAGE), met level (the level it was created at, not the level it happens to be when this save runs), met game (VERSION_EMERALD), and poke ball (ITEM_POKE_BALL), same as friendship -- but only where there is no record to retain: a new file's empty slot, or a slot whose personality/OT id says it now holds a different Pokemon. OT name, met location, and OT gender still file zero even there: they need the current save's player identity and map, which to_save_pokemon has no way to see. The cached stat block (max_hp/attack/.../special_defense) and current HP belong to the battler, which adopts them verbatim from the loaded record (party::from_save_pokemon, through battle::BattlePokemon::with_cached_stats and with_saved_experience: upstream's LoadPlayerParty copies the record and calls nothing, :170-178, so a record whose level byte, experience word and cache disagree stays as saved until the next CalculateMonStats), and the merge writes them straight back from battle::BattlePokemon::cached_stats (never Deoxys's live Speed Forme view) and the live HP, with no recomputation and no session offset: only a level-up replaces the cache, EV-aware, inside battle::BattlePokemon::raise_level_to_experience, moving HP by the signed max-HP delta (fainted stays 0, Shedinja stays 1). So Continue then SAVE is byte-exact at any stored hp, in-session damage subtracts from the stored value, a level-up files the new cache and HP, and repeated saves file the same bytes (pinned by continue_then_save_keeps_a_full_health_ev_trained_lead_at_full, battle_damage_subtracts_from_the_saved_hp and a_level_up_moves_saved_hp_by_the_ev_aware_max_hp_delta_and_saves_stably in crates/pokeemerald-rs/src/party/tests/merge_hp.rs, and saving_twice_in_one_session_files_the_same_bytes in crates/pokeemerald-rs/src/flow/save_continue_hp_tests.rs). A record that cannot retain bytes falls back to party::to_save_pokemon, which files the same cache and HP. Pinned by re_saving_an_untouched_lead_writes_the_record_back_byte_for_byte and re_saving_a_loaded_mon_keeps_every_field_the_battle_model_does_not_carry in crates/pokeemerald-rs/src/party/tests/retained_record.rs and by a_re_saved_continued_lead_keeps_the_bytes_no_battle_model_carries in crates/pokeemerald-rs/src/flow/save_continue_party_tests.rs. A second deliberate divergence sits on the no-lead arm of the save half: it does not unconditionally zero slot 0. When the load's decode refused slot 0 (recorded in OverworldPhase::undecodable_lead_retained, set by load_lead_from_save's error arm), the save leaves save1.player_party[0] and save1.player_party_count exactly as loaded instead of writing engine::save::Pokemon::default() and a zero count, so a failed secure-region checksum -- or any other party::PartyError, such as an unknown species -- does not cost the player the whole record (nickname, OT name, language, markings, and the secure bytes themselves) on the very next ordinary SAVE. Upstream needs no such arm because its wholesale gSaveBlock1Ptr->playerParty[i] = gPlayerParty[i] copy achieves the same preservation for free: a Bad Egg (src/pokemon.c:3742-3744 and :4167-4169 set boxMon->isBadEgg = TRUE on a checksum mismatch and leave the mon in gPlayerParty) rides that copy with playerPartyCount unchanged, and LoadPlayerParty validates nothing, so the count rides through the next load too. This port needs the explicit flag only because its decode is a real decode that can refuse where upstream's memcpy cannot, but the save side does not branch on it either way: a genuinely empty slot (playerPartyCount == 0 at load) takes the exact same untouched-bytes arm as a retained-undecodable one, since ZeroPlayerPartyMons is NewGameInitData's and the battle facilities' own reset (new_game.c:143,156,181; battle_factory.c:289,430; battle_tent.c:274; recorded_battle.c:529), never called from the continue/save path. The flag itself survives only as a diagnostic record of why the phase has no lead (OverworldPhase::undecodable_lead_retained's own docs), not as a save-time decision input. Pinned by a_slot_that_will_not_decode_survives_an_ordinary_save, a_deliberate_identity_change_overrides_a_retained_undecodable_slot and a_genuinely_empty_partys_residual_slot_survives_an_ordinary_save in crates/pokeemerald-rs/src/flow/save_continue_retention_tests.rs.

SaveObjectEvents.reason: SaveObjectEvents/LoadObjectEvents (:180-194) copy all OBJECT_EVENTS_COUNT entries of gObjectEvents in and out of SaveBlock1::objectEvents. This port models the direction and elevation bytes of one entry: objectEvents[OBJ_EVENT_ID_PLAYER]'s facingDirection/movementDirection nibbles (0xA30 + 0x18), each written from PlayerState's own field, which ShowStartMenu's StopPlayerAvatar (start_menu.c:581-588, field_player_avatar.c:1223-1228, event_object_movement.c:2361-2371) resets to the facing direction before any save (a save opened on a slide's landing frame stores the locked facing in both nibbles), and currentElevation/previousElevation nibbles (0xA30 + 0x0B, include/global.fieldmap.h:232-233) plus the active bit (0xA30 bit 0) and a port marker in the top bit of the third bitfield byte (0xA30+0x03 bit 7, inside the padding:4 upstream leaves unused, include/global.fieldmap.h:224), as engine::save::SavedObjectEvent, written by OverworldPhase::copy_party_and_objects_to_save and read back on continue (facingDirection and the elevation pair are restored, the loaded movementDirection is ignored and PlayerState starts in step with facing; elevations: a continue restores the pair verbatim, so history retained on multi-level and transition cells survives, and the saved pair is trusted only when the player object is active -- either a record this port's writer marked (its marker is the strong signal) or a pristine upstream record with no marker whose active and isPlayer (0xA30+0x02 bit 0, include/global.fieldmap.h:212) bits are set, whose padding:4 bits are zero and whose pair neither holds the multi-level value ObjectEventUpdateElevation never assigns -- and its current elevation is one ObjectEventUpdateElevation could hold on the landing cell (the cell's own elevation, or anything on a multi-level cell); the marker is set only by this port's writer, and the writer also stores the object's currentCoords (0xA30+0x10, include/global.fieldmap.h:235) as SaveBlock1::pos plus MAP_OFFSET (7), which a decode requires to match pos, so a pair left behind by an earlier port writer that moved pos while preserving the entry (for example after a downgrade and upgrade) is not trusted either, marked or not; the save also stamps the save counter its write carries into the entry's initialCoords bytes (0xA30+0x0C, include/global.fieldmap.h:234, unmodeled and untouched by that earlier writer), and SaveStore::load trusts a marked pair only when the stamp equals the loaded slot's counter (an unmarked pristine upstream record carries no port stamp, its initialCoords being upstream's own spawn coordinates, so it is not held to one), so a marked record an earlier writer preserved while advancing the counter (for example a walk off and back to the same coordinates under a writer that did not restamp it) is not trusted either, while this writer restamps every save; an unmarked image that is not a pristine upstream record (coordinates disagreeing with pos, isPlayer clear, padding bits set, or an illegal pair) falls back to the tile's arrival elevation. RESIDUAL: unmarked records are not reliably identifiable -- an upstream-origin image that an earlier port writer re-saved at an unchanged pos keeps matching coordinates, isPlayer, zero padding and a legal pair, so it is indistinguishable from the upstream record and is adopted with whatever pair the image held (the continue's landing-cell holdability check is the only remaining filter). A settled player never holds a mismatch on an ordinary cell, since a finished step shifts previous coords to current (ShiftStillObjectEventCoords, event_object_movement.c:2162) before DoGroundEffects_OnFinishStep re-runs ObjectEventUpdateElevation (:8120-8130); the mid-step multi-level early return does not survive to a save). That is the only part of the array a continue observably restores here -- SpawnObjectEventsOnReturnToField respawns the player from it (event_object_movement.c:1715-1726) -- and it replaces the earlier DIR_SOUTH stand-in. NOT modelled: the other bytes of the player's entry (sprite ids, ground-effect and movement bitfields including facingDirectionLocked, coordinate history, metatile-behaviour history, movementActionId) and every non-player entry, because this workspace models no object-event system to hold them; a save block whose byte is DIR_NONE still falls back to GetAdjustedInitialDirection.

clear_sav.reason: ClearSav1/ClearSav2's zero-the-blocks-when-a-new-game-starts effect is modelled by SaveStore::clear_base, applied on every write of a new-game session (#230 review; #232 review round two). Upstream settles a new game's RAM once -- NewGameInitData memsets gSaveBlock1 via ClearSav1 (new_game.c:160, load_save.c:64-67, which also covers ResetGameStats's gSaveBlock1Ptr->gameStats) and resets gSaveBlock2's deferred state field by field (encryption key :155, ResetPokedex, PlayTimeCounter_Reset), with Sav2_ClearSetDefault -> ClearSav2 on top when the boot load found nothing usable (intro.c:1155-1156) -- and HandleSavingData then writes a whole slot out of that RAM (save.c:736-739) on every save of the session. This port defers unmodelled bytes to the image on disk, so it re-applies the reset per write, and the clear_base input is a property of the *session* (OverworldPhase::new_game_session, read at the store call as game_save::SaveLineage), never of the save mode: keying it off the save type left a new-game session's SAVE_NORMAL retry -- the arm a cleared gDifferentSaveFile produces after a failed overwrite -- writing the replaced trainer's deferred bytes back out. NOT modelled: the RAM struct pointers/shuffling (SetSaveBlocksPointers, MoveSaveBlocks_ResetHeap) and the checksum globals. optionsTextSpeed/optionsWindowFrameType's own boot-verdict carrying is flow::new_game_options_for's contract (issue #1125), not clear_base's; other still-unmodelled SaveBlock2 bytes (e.g. localTimeOffset) remain a real gap, since clear_base drops them with the rest of the deferred payload regardless of boot verdict.

CgbModVol.reason: CgbModVol's envelope-goal/sustain-goal resolution re-implemented as cgb_envelope::cgb_envelope_goal + CgbEnvelope::new/latch_goal, folded in only at note-on and each envelopeCounter==0 boundary via step_with_goal/step_frame; a live track-volume write (CgbVoice::set_track_volume) queues the routing state alone and never latches directly (issue #1210, S-3 slice 2).

CgbOscOff.reason: CgbOscOff's channel-1/2 off-write is reimplemented as SquareChannel::apply_hardware_off_write (crates/audio/src/psg.rs, reached through CgbVoice::apply_hardware_off_write): REG_NR14/REG_NR24 = 0x80 (m4a.c:857-868) clears the frequency register's high three bits, so GBAudioWriteNR14/NR24's catch-up (mgba/src/gb/audio.c:140-194,219-241) rates a later idle-duty advance against the low byte alone rather than the note's last full frequency. The write is also a genuine hardware trigger (GBAudioWriteNR14, mgba/src/gb/audio.c:168-186): it reloads channel 1's sweep from the truncated frequency, rechecks overflow, and revives a muted channel, as SquareChannel::retrigger does. Mixer applies it the instant a Square1/Square2 slot idles, both on TrackStop's immediate clear (src/m4a_1.s#TrackStop) and on natural envelope retirement, tracking the truncated duty position independently of the CgbVoice occupant so the next note-on continues it. NR12=8 leaves the DAC on, so a nonzero-shift channel-1 sweep keeps ticking at 128 Hz and retuning the played frequency while the slot idles (mgba/src/gb/audio.c:965-988); Mixer::mix_frame steps the vacated slot's sweep at the frame's shared tick offsets through CgbVoice::advance_idle_duty, and a sweep overflow mutes the idle channel so its frequency freezes. The idle channel's envelope is dead (volume 0), so GBAudioRun skips its duty catch-up at frame and sweep ticks (mgba/src/gb/audio.c:493-510); the duty catch-up is deferred (SquareChannel::defer_idle_samples) and rated once at the next note-on at the frequency the sweep finally reached. The channel's envelope-silencing half (REG_NR12/REG_NR22/REG_NR42 = 8) remains a byproduct of CgbEnvelope::retire when a note's envelope ends, not a dedicated write; channel 4's noise off-write (NR42 = 8; NR44 = 0x80, m4a.c:873-874) is modeled as a zero-volume preserving retrigger: CgbVoice::apply_hardware_off_write zeroes the hardware volume (HardwareEnvelopeVolume::write_off) and restarts the LFSR and phase (NoiseChannel::retrigger) but leaves the output latch ch4.sample alone, which only an LFSR clock (mgba/src/gb/audio.c:641, lsb * currentVolume) or an envelope step (audio.c:730-732) re-resolves. Mixer applies it on retirement and TrackStop, and the vacated slot keeps its noise clock and phase running and emits the latch through CgbVoice::render_idle_hardware until the first zero-volume clock settles it, so a note triggered inside that period inherits the predecessor's volume-resolved level (NoiseChannel::continue_output_from, 0..=15, never inferred from the predecessor's current volume), rendered against the volume it was resolved at, but only after the replacement's note-on NR43 writes have clocked the held predecessor: NoiseChannel::inherit_hardware_from keeps its whole channel state, and once the initial trigger commits NoiseChannel::commit_initial_writes settles its owed clocks, then installs the replacement's width and clocks the elapsed time at the fastest rate (the width-only write, m4a.c:1020-1022, then the pitched write, m4a.c:1197-1202; mgba/src/gb/audio.c:354-383,602-644) at the predecessor's hardware volume, so the latch left by that catch-up (not the unclocked level) is what the new note holds until its own first clock; the exception is a note that retires on its first envelope pass (zero sustain, no pseudo-echo): m4a.c jumps from the start block to oscillator_off (m4a.c:1040,1090-1102,1125-1129) and never reaches the pitched write, so commit_initial_writes keeps the width-only rate and the off-write restarts channel 4 at that rate rather than the requested pitch; a replacement cancelled before its first pass never consumes the held state; with Mixer::is_idle counting the unsettled idle latch so a fade-end stop does not truncate the tail; channel 3's disable (REG_NR30 = 0, m4a.c:869-871) stops the wave clock but clears neither the held sample nor NR51 (GBAudioWriteNR30, mgba/src/gb/audio.c:246-253), so CgbVoice::render_idle_hardware keeps emitting the vacated wave slot's held latch (WaveChannel::held_output) on the last committed route without advancing its wave-RAM rotation, on both retirement and TrackStop, for as long as the mixer renders frames, until a replacement note takes the slot (Mixer::is_idle deliberately ignores the held level, so a finished song or fade stops being mixed rather than holding a never-settling level open); the wave length counter (#2900) remains unmodeled.

CgbPan.reason: CgbPan's hard-pan-vs-centre decision re-implemented as cgb_envelope::cgb_pan (S-3 slice 2).

CgbSound.reason: CgbSound's per-hardware-channel envelope, oscillator, and pan loop is re-implemented as cgb_voice::CgbVoice, driven from Mixer::mix_frame. The envelope phase machine, including the pseudoEchoLength pseudo-echo tail (m4a.c:900-1204), is CgbEnvelope. Every CGB_CHANNEL_MO_VOL write CgbSound applies as an NRx4 bit-7 trigger for channels 1, 2, and 4 (m4a.c:1206-1226) -- the envelope phase transitions at m4a.c:1060-1069, 1090-1099, 1125-1137, and 1150-1158, and the live track volume/pan or tremolo LFO write at m4a_1.s:1391-1400 -- re-triggers the oscillator, via CgbEnvelope::step/step_frame/note_off and CgbVoice::set_track_volume reporting the write and CgbVoice::begin_frame applying it through Oscillator::retrigger. A frame that retires the voice applies neither that retrigger nor the NR51 pan commit: its oscillator_off/channel_complete jump (m4a.c:1053-1056, 1084-1101) bypasses the whole CGB_CHANNEL_MO_VOL block (m4a.c:1205-1226), so a volume or pan write pending on the retiring frame never reaches the route the retained hardware keeps; a note's first pass keeps its start-block duty and sweep writes (m4a.c:997-1002) but not its pitch: a first pass that retires at once (zero attack, decay, sustain, and echo volume; m4a.c:1031-1040, 1090-1102, 1125-1129, 1150-1162) skips the NRx3/NRx4 pitch write (m4a.c:1197-1202) and the volume-block trigger (m4a.c:1205-1226), so CgbVoice::begin_frame issues no square retrigger and SquareChannel::commit_initial_writes keeps the replaced note's frequency register and duty clock under the incoming duty and sweep control, and the off-write (m4a.c:857-868) truncates that register to its low byte, clearing the high frequency bits. That volume block writes NR14 without NR13 (m4a.c:1219-1225; the pitch block at m4a.c:1198 is NR13's only writer), so channel 1's sweep reloads from the note's high bits rejoined to whatever low byte the sweep has reached, and channel 4's LFSR and clock phase reset. A failing sweep overflow check stops the hardware channel alone: CgbSound holds SOUND_CHANNEL_SF_ON for the note's whole envelope (m4a.c:1055-1058 is its only clearer), so CgbVoice stops its oscillator rather than retiring the note and a later safe trigger revives it. A trigger-time overflow (mgba audio.c:180-186) is not modelled that way: mGBA re-latches ch1.sample from the new duty position and initial volume at the trigger (audio.c:193), but CgbVoice still renders silence for it. A pitch write to a stopped square (length-expired or sweep-overflowed) re-latches the held level its NR14 catch-up reaches (mgba audio.c:162-169, 219-224). An overflow at a 128 Hz sweep tick on a still-playing square only clears playingCh1 (mgba audio.c:667-672), GBAudioRun then skips the channel (audio.c:493), and GBAudioSamplePSG keeps mixing the untouched ch1.sample (audio.c:745-754), so CgbVoice::render_clocked holds last_contribution at the duty level at the overflow tick, which the channel was caught up to before the sweep step (mgba audio.c:657, 667-672) and which is read before the sweep's frequency write-back rather than taken from the last rendered sample, through a later length expiry, until the next trigger or off-write catch-up. A note whose note-off arrives before its first CgbSound pass takes the SF_START | SF_STOP short-circuit to oscillator_off, retiring at once past the modify/CgbModVol write rather than running the release ramp or the pseudo-echo tail (m4a.c:988-996, 1040-1047, 1053-1057): CgbEnvelope::note_off records the request into the Starting phase and CgbEnvelope::start applies it on that pass, reporting no retrigger. Channel 3 volume follows gCgb3Vol into NR32 (m4a.c:1205-1211); upstream indexes that 16-byte table unchecked and a centred CgbModVol goal reaches level 31, so levels 16-31 read the adjacent gClockTable bytes 0x00-0x0F (m4a_tables.c:168-177, adjacent in the built ROM), which clear NR32's volume bits and 75% bit and mute the wave, modelled as an explicit 32-entry NR32_BY_LEVEL table decoded by nr32_wave_gain_256: the wave nibble is integer-shifted before centering, so quarter, half, and three-quarter volume quantize neighbouring nibbles together as the hardware does. Channel 3 reloads wave RAM only when the programmable-wave asset identity changes (m4a.c:1003-1012): a note on the same wave, whether it replaces the sounding note or follows retirement, keeps the rotation the prior note left (WaveChannel::continue_rotation_from through Oscillator::carry_hardware_state_from) and restarts only trigger timing, while a different wave loads its table unrotated. A track pitch write is held as a pending request and committed at CgbVoice::begin_frame only when the envelope has not retired: CgbSound's retirement jump to oscillator_off/channel_complete (m4a.c:1053-1056) bypasses the pitch block (m4a.c:1194-1203), so a pitch change on the retiring frame never reaches the retained hardware that the off-write truncates and that later notes continue from.  The sound-length counters of all four channels are modelled (psg::LengthCounter, 64 steps for channels 1, 2, and 4 and 256 for channel 3; CgbVoice's cgb_voice/length.rs): the first pass stores the instrument's length into NRx1 (channels 1, 2, and 4 load 64 minus its low six bits; channel 3's NR31 is covered below) and sets the NRx4 length-enable bit only for a nonzero length (m4a.c:1001, 1014-1018, 1021-1028; m4a_1.s:1771-1772), the channel 1, 2, and 4 pitch block's no-trigger NRx4 store can take the enable-edge extra clock on an even frame-sequencer step (m4a.c:1197-1203; mgba audio.c:172-178), and every channel 1, 2, and 4 CGB_CHANNEL_MO_VOL trigger reloads the counter only from zero, to 64 or 63 for an enabled counter owing the extra clock (m4a.c:1219-1226; mgba audio.c:187-192). The shared psg::FrameSequencer clocks length at 256 Hz on steps 0, 2, 4, and 6 beside the 128 Hz sweep (mgba audio.c:649-707); a counter that reaches zero stops the oscillator output, LFSR, and hardware envelope while the output holds its last level and a square's duty position is caught up by the next register write (mgba audio.c:162-171, 493-510, 781-789); a square's last level is its duty level at the expiry sample, because GBAudioUpdateFrame runs channels 1-3 to the frame-event timestamp before the length clock clears them (mgba audio.c:649-657, 678-684), so the square's level is re-latched at the tick, ahead of a coincident sweep retune (SquareChannel::held_level via CgbVoice::expiry_square_latch), while channel 4 is outside that 0x7 run (mgba audio.c:585) and holds the sample before the expiry, and leaves the note's software envelope, gate, and EndTie eligibility untouched, so on channels 1, 2, and 4 a later transition or live-volume trigger plays it again for a fresh count. A replacement inherits the predecessor's counter and enable bit until its own NRx1 store, and the channel 1, 2, and 4 idle off-write clears the enable bit and reloads only a zero count. Channel 3 stores its whole length byte into NR31, loading 256 minus it, and keeps NR34 bit 6 for a nonzero length, with bit 7 set until the volume block clears it (m4a.c:1014-1018, 1213-1216; mgba audio.c:255-258, 290-313): the first pitch block's NR34 store is therefore the wave's only trigger (it takes the enable-edge extra clock and reloads a zero count to 256, or 255 when owed the extra clock), later envelope transitions and live volume writes only rewrite NR32 and so never revive an expired wave counter, and CgbOscOff(3) writes NR30 alone, leaving the count and enable bit. A wave stopped by its counter presents the latch its last clock left (CgbVoice::render_clocked through Oscillator::held_wave_contribution; mgba audio.c:768-774), and a vacated wave slot keeps counting its preserved counter through CgbVoice::render_idle_hardware (mgba audio.c:690-696). The sequencer epoch (step 6 before the first sample) preserves the established sweep offsets and is not mGBA's boot phase. That NRx1 store is the 8-bit sum (duty << 6) + length (m4a.c:1001), so a square re-selects its duty from bits 6-7 of the summed byte and loads the counter from bits 0-5 (mgba audio.c:885-888; SquareChannel::write_nrx1), while the enable bit still follows the raw instrument length. A pitch write to a stopped square latches the held level its NR14 store's catch-up reaches before the high byte lands: NR13's catch-up runs at the old rate and NR14's at the intermediate frequency (new low byte, old high bits), and nothing runs the stopped channel after the store (pokeemerald m4a.c:1197-1203; mgba audio.c:162-171, 219-224, 493-501; SquareChannel::set_frequency_latching). A retired wave slot keeps mixing its held sample on the last committed NR51 route, since NR30 = 0 clears neither (m4a.c:869-871; mgba audio.c:246-253, 768-774), and nothing an idle slot does settles it: only a retrigger (the incoming voice's initial trigger drops the stale hardware) or a route write ends it, and discarding the mixer, as a MusicPlayer restart does, drops it. CgbVoice::holds_wave_output reports a nonzero, routed held level. It is deliberately outside the finite-tail predicate Mixer::is_idle / Sequencer::is_sounding / Sequencer::is_finished (an indefinitely held level would keep a wave song from ever finishing); the literal conservative output query is Mixer::has_held_wave_output / Mixer::is_silent / Sequencer::is_silent. NR52 power-off is not modelled. A wave note whose first pass retires at once (zero attack, decay, sustain, and echo volume) still reports an envelope boundary but jumps through oscillator_off past the NR51 store (m4a.c:1053-1056, 1205-1208), so CgbVoice::carry_hardware_state_from keeps the predecessor's committed route (StereoRouting::carry_committed_route_from) and CgbVoice::begin_frame commits a wave's pan at a boundary only while the envelope survives; the slot's held wave sample stays on the predecessor's route, while a replacement that survives its first pass commits its own.  Channels 1, 2, and 4 take the same retiring first pass past the NR51 store (m4a.c:1053-1056, 1205-1208) as the wave, but their constructed pan stays committed because the retained route is never audible: a vacated square slot emits nothing and only keeps its duty running (CgbVoice::render_idle_hardware), and a first-pass-retiring noise replacement's width-only NR43 write and NR42 = 8 off-write leave the channel clocking at hardware volume zero (m4a.c:873-874, 1020-1022; mgba audio.c:371-383, 602-644), so its first LFSR clock resolves the inherited latch to zero before the first idle sample and no route carries it; a noise replacement that survives its first pass commits its own route (m4a.c:1081-1082, 1205-1208).

MPlayExtender.reason: MPlayExtender's square-channel power-on triggers are modelled: REG_NR12/REG_NR22 = 0x8 and REG_NR14/REG_NR24 = 0x80 (m4a.c:268-273) trigger Square1 and Square2 at frequency 0 with the DAC on before any note, so their duty index free-runs from the start. Mixer::new seeds the Square1/Square2 idle hardware with CgbVoice::initialized_square_hardware, Mixer::mix_frame advances it through CgbVoice::render_idle_hardware, and the first note's Mixer::add_cgb_voice inherits the elapsed duty phase through CgbVoice::carry_hardware_state_from, as mGBA's GBAudioRun catches the index up on a register write (mgba/src/gb/audio.c:162-171,493-510). Not modelled: SOUNDCNT_X/SOUNDCNT_L/NR50 master setup, the NR42/NR44 noise triggers (a freshly started noise channel's latch is already zero), NR30 wave-off, and the SoundInfo ident handshake, which the port has no register state for.
