Each step's volX (m4a.c:756) reaches Sequencer::render_frame_with_fade, which stages it across that frame's ticks and only then re-derives each surviving track's volume through TrkVolPitSet's Rust port (sequencer::track_volume, m4a.c:772), before Mixer::mix_frame sums voices and wraps the DirectSound sum to a signed byte, mod 256 (m4a_1.s:308-339; issue #1243): matching upstream's per-track-then-wrap order instead of the earlier clip-then-scale shortcut that diverged on multi-voice frames that overflow the mix, and matching TrkVolPitSet's single deferred, post-tick propagation (m4a_1.s:1361-1400), which ply_pan and the other volume commands only flag (MPT_FLG_VOLCHG) rather than applying mid-tick -- so neither a track whose Fine lands in that frame nor an intervening PAN receives the step, mirroring ply_fine's flag clear (m4a_1.s:750-777). The terminal step that reaches volX 0 instead stops every surviving track outright through Mixer::stop_track, which now drops every matching DirectSound or CGB slot immediately, matching TrackStop's immediate channel clear (m4a_1.s:1469-1506) rather than continuing through TrkVolPitSet -- for CGB this forces the oscillator silent on that same frame instead of leaving it to the next latched envelope-goal boundary. That step also latches Sequencer's paused state, upstream's MUSICPLAYER_STATUS_PAUSE (m4a.c:740): the sequencer never ticks or restarts again, while App::advance_music keeps rendering frames through Mixer::mix_frame until the mixer falls silent -- the master-mix reverb ring's delayed samples and any voice an already-ended track left in release -- matching SoundMain/SoundMainRAM_Reverb running regardless of the pause (m4a_1.s:20-119) rather than truncating that tail (issue #1281). FADE_IN (m4aMPlayFadeIn, m4a.c:219-227) and TEMPORARY_FADE (m4aMPlayFadeOutTemporarily, m4a.c:207) are NOT implemented and stay pending on src/m4a.c.

MPlayMain.reason: MPlayMain's tempo-tick loop and its single once-per-frame post-loop MPT_FLG_VOLCHG/MPT_FLG_PITCHG propagation pass reimplemented as Sequencer::advance_frame/do_tick/propagate_dirty_tracks, gated on TrackState::vol_dirty/pitch_dirty (set by VOL/PAN/pitch/ModType/LFO, consumed by Fine and by a successful Note, matching ply_note's own flag mask); FadeOutBody's pre-tick volX write is staged the same way via Sequencer::stage_fade_volume. Its per-track command loop has no termination cap, as upstream's (m4a_1.s:1232-1284): a zero-wait run of any length reaches its next Wait or Fine. Unlike the hardware, which spends the whole CPU on it, Sequencer::process_track yields after TRACK_COMMANDS_PER_TICK commands so render_frame stays bounded, and the logical tick is suspended (Sequencer::suspended_tick): the next frame resumes it at the same command before anything else, adding no tempo, expiring no gate again, running no later track, and applying no dirty volume or pitch until the tick and that frame's remaining ticks finish, so the tick stays atomic as upstream's (m4a_1.s:1173-1360); the song is delayed by the yielded frames. The run is ended only when a BurstProbe finds the track and MEMACC state identical to an earlier one (probes of other tracks are cleared when a track writes the shared MEMACC area, and the snapshot schedule restarts rather than freezing), i.e. it can never progress. A never-repeating, never-yielding loop keeps consuming its per-frame budget, as it would hang upstream. A frame that ends with the tick suspended does not mix (Sequencer::mix_committed_frame): it renders silence and leaves the mixer untouched, because SoundMain mixes only after MPlayMainHead returns (m4a_1.s:51-62), so no note started or released part-way through the tick is heard before the tick completes. A fade step handed to a frame whose tick is suspended waits for the tick to complete (Sequencer::pending_fade): FadeOutBody runs only when the next MPlayMain begins (m4a_1.s:1152-1169), so the step is staged, or the terminal step pauses, after the tick's last command and before the next frame's tick, and every note of one tick shares one volX.

RealClearChain.reason: RealClearChain (m4a_1.s:726-748), called only from ply_fine, unlinks a channel from its track's chain and stores 0 into chan->track (m4a_1.s:744-745), an early no-op if already untracked. Voice::detach_track (voice.rs) reimplements the track-nulling half via Mixer::release_track (issue #1192); the linked-list unlink itself is not modeled, since Mixer owns voices in its own slot array rather than a track-owned chain.

SoundMainRAM_BoundaryInterpolation.reason: SoundMainRAM's per-output linear interpolation reads the sample one past the current index for its final step before a loop wraps or a one-shot retires (m4a_1.s:399-407), which is the encoded byte wav2agb's payload writer emits past an agbl-trimmed logical count. Voice::render's next-sample lookahead in crates/audio/src/voice.rs reads that retained guard from the pack sample while WaveData's logical length still drives the loop and retirement boundary; crates/xtask/src/extract/wav.rs (extraction) and crates/rom-import/src/domains/audio.rs (ROM import) both keep exactly one guard past sample_count so the runtime has it (PR #1445, issue #1342).

SoundMainRAM_Exhaustion.reason: SoundMainRAM's shared post-advance exhaustion test, reached by both the TONEDATA_TYPE_FIX path and the pitch-scaled path: the remaining-sample-count subtraction sits after the phase advance inside the per-output DMA loop (m4a_1.s:406-420, subs r2, r2, lr; ble _081DD134) and the non-looping arm stores statusFlags = 0 immediately rather than deferring to the next SoundMainRAM pass (m4a_1.s:376-386, _081DD158.._081DD174). Voice::render re-checks termination immediately after advance_wrapping and retires a non-looping voice in that same render call instead of waiting for a later output slot's pre-render normalize() to catch it, or missing it entirely when the crossing lands in the accumulator's last slot (issue #1078). Still not modelled: SoundMainRAM_ChanLoop's own envelope attack/decay/sustain/release stepping (m4a_1.s ~_081DCF6A-_081DD03A, no separate ledger artifact yet), the PCM DMA ring-buffer's packed four-lane layout via ror 8 (upstream's lanes never carry into each other, since each voice term is masked to a lane's top byte at m4a_1.s:308-339 and :395-416; this crate accumulates each output independently in an i32 and Mixer::mix_frame wraps the finished sum to a signed byte, mod 256, which is the same result), and the raw currentPointer/count pointer bookkeeping beyond the exhaustion test itself. Voice's phase advance clears only bits 23-29 after counting whole samples (bic r9, r9, 0x3F800000, m4a_1.s:415-418), so phase bits 30-31 persist into the next advance and into the interpolation product, which multiplies the whole retained word in wrapping 32-bit arithmetic before the asr 23 (mul lr, r9, r1; add lr, r0, lr, asr 23, m4a_1.s:403-404); a phase kept below 2^23 plus a step under 127 source samples per output sample never sets them.

SoundMainRAM_Reverb.reason: SoundMainRAM's reverb arm (feedback delay line seeding the mix buffer before per-voice mixing) reimplemented as Reverb, wired into Mixer::mix_frame; a song's SongHeader::reverb level enables it via Song::with_reverb/Sequencer::with_config (issue #185). Mixer::mix_frame wraps each DirectSound sample to a signed byte (mod 256, no carry between lanes, matching the masked top-byte lane adds at m4a_1.s:308-339 and :395-416) and commits that DirectSound-only frame to Reverb before CGB voices render, matching SoundMainRAM_Reverb's exclusive DirectSound pcmBuffer feed (m4a_1.s:88-119) and CgbSound's separate NRxx hardware-register path (m4a.c:925-1226); CGB output is mixed in only afterward, for the final output buffer, and never reaches the delay ring (issue #1230).

TONEDATA_TYPE_FIX.reason: SoundMainRAM's fixed-rate DirectSound branch (m4a_1.s:498: tst TONEDATA_TYPE_FIX; movne r8, 0x800000 forces a 1:1 phase step) reimplemented as Voice::fixed_rate forcing the phase step to pitch::FRAC_ONE, which also reproduces the branch's un-interpolated raw-sample reads as a side effect (S-3 slice 3). Covers only this FIX branch, not the rest of SoundMainRAM; the shared post-advance exhaustion test is src/m4a_1.s#SoundMainRAM_Exhaustion. The separate CGB-side use of the flag (m4a.c:1184-1202 8-bit-DAC frequency rounding) is implemented too, recorded on src/m4a.c#TONEDATA_TYPE_FIX (cgb_voice::DacCorrection::apply, PR #276).

TrackStop.reason: Mixer::stop_track reimplements TrackStop's immediate channel teardown: dropping each matching DirectSound or CGB slot absorbs the active-channel status clear (m4a_1.s:1480-1493), the per-channel owner unlink (m4a_1.s:1494-1498), and the track channel-head clear (m4a_1.s:1499-1500). The CGB oscillator-off call itself (src/m4a.c#CgbOscOff) is applied to a vacated Square1/Square2 slot before it drops, truncating the frequency its idle duty catch-up rates against (issue #1482).  Mixer::stop_track leaves a vacated wave slot's held sample mixing, since the CgbOscOff call TrackStop makes for each active CGB channel (m4a_1.s:1484-1491) writes only NR30 = 0 for wave (m4a.c:857-870), which clears neither the sample nor NR51 (mgba audio.c:246-253, 768-774). That level is permanent, so it is excluded from the finite-tail predicate Mixer::is_idle (and Sequencer::is_sounding / is_finished, which would otherwise never finish after a wave note) and reported by Mixer::has_held_wave_output / Mixer::is_silent / Sequencer::is_silent; a new wave voice's initial trigger in the slot ends it.

ply_endtie.reason: ply_endtie (m4a_1.s:1819-1857) walks a track's channel list picking the first channel matching the played key with SOUND_CHANNEL_SF_START|SF_ENV set and SF_STOP clear, then sets SF_STOP on it alone (issue #901). Reimplemented as Mixer::note_off_track, which instead scans every DirectSound and CGB slot on the track for the requested key and releases the one with the greatest note-on ordinal (mixer.rs note_off_track), a newest-wins equivalent rather than upstream's list-order walk. The CGB side of that eligibility test is now phase-accurate: CgbVoice::is_end_tie_eligible (delegating to CgbEnvelope::is_end_tie_eligible) excludes an automatic pseudo-echo tail and a retired channel, matching ply_endtie's START|ENV/~STOP test, since an automatic zero-sustain tail clears SOUND_CHANNEL_SF_ENV before setting only SF_IEC and never SF_STOP (m4a.c:1090-1098, 1125-1129) and so upstream skips it. DirectSound has no such divergence (m4a_1.s:228-250 keeps SF_ENV set through its own automatic tail) and keeps the plain non-stopping test. Deferred: the list-order-walk mechanism itself and its single-match-then-stop short-circuit are not modeled; note_off_track's newest-ordinal selection is a standing simplification predating this fix.

ply_fine.reason: ply_fine (m4a_1.s:750-777) sets SOUND_CHANNEL_SF_STOP on every still-on channel of the finished track, then unconditionally clears each channel via RealClearChain before resetting the track's flags. It walks track->chan, the single chain ply_note's insertion code (m4a_1.s:1719-1731) shares between SoundChannel and CgbChannel entries (identical track/prev/next offsets, m4a_constants.inc:132-134,251-253), so it also nulls a finished track's CGB channel. Mixer::release_track reimplements the SoundChannel half via Voice::detach_track (issue #1192): select_direct_sound_slot's released-slot tie-break sorts a null owner below every live-owned voice, matching chan->track's null-pointer ordering in ply_note's DirectSound victim loop (m4a_1.s:1694-1711). The CGB half is left attached: not presently player-visible, since add_cgb_voice's reusable test short-circuits on occupant.is_stopping() before ever comparing track (mixer.rs:192-198), and release_track already note-offs a matching CGB voice before returning. Deferred: giving CgbVoice the same nullable ownership, and the doubly-linked chain removal mechanism itself, since Mixer scans its own slot array rather than a linked list.

ply_note.reason: ply_note (m4a_1.s:1538) key-split (TONEDATA_TYPE_SPL) / rhythm (TONEDATA_TYPE_RHY) child resolution, including the pre-allocation no-note path for a nested key-split/rhythm child (m4a_1.s:1604-1609) and, with no upstream equivalent, for an empty child slot (issue #1304), the TONEDATA_TYPE_FIX dispatch bypass, and the pseudoEchoVolume/Length note-on snapshot are reimplemented as sequencer::resolve_instrument + note_on (S-3 slice 3). The channel search is now implemented too (issue #314): sequencer::note_priority sums the song header's priority and the track's PRIO saturated at 0xFF (m4a_1.s:1628-1633) and mixer::Mixer::add_voice/add_cgb_voice reuse a free or released channel, else steal the lowest-priority channel the newcomer outranks (equal priority tie-broken by track order), else refuse the note (m4a_1.s:1647-1718, :1744-1745). The Square1 sweep normalization of the CGB store path is implemented too: sequencer::admitted_sweep_byte replaces ToneData::pan_sweep with 0x08 when bit 7 is set or no bit of 0x70 is set, before CgbVoice::square_with_fixed_rate decodes it (m4a_1.s:1773-1783). The CGB store path (m4a_1.s:1766-1772) copies ToneData::length into CgbChannel::length (:1771-1772), and the length reaches the Square1, Square2, Wave, and Noise voices as the NRx1 (NR31 for the wave) sound length and the NRx4 length-enable bit (cgb_voice::CgbVoice::with_length). Still deferred: SoundChannel::count is not seeded from track->unk_3C (:1792-1793). The track-local tone's ADSR snapshot is implemented too: sequencer::note_on applies the track's xATTA/xDECA/xSUST/xRELE overrides (sequencer::adsr_override::AdsrOverride) over a direct tone's ADSR for DirectSound and CGB notes (m4a_1.s:1750-1758), but not over a key-split or rhythm child, which ply_note reads from the bank (m4a_1.s:1580-1609); ply_voice's tone copy is modelled by Event::Voice clearing the overrides (m4a_1.s:945-965). xWAVE/xTYPE stay unexecuted.

ply_patt.reason: ply_patt (m4a_1.s:851-869) pushes the return cursor onto track->patternStack and jumps to the target; at the engine's depth of 3 it branches to ply_fine without reading the target. Reimplemented three times: the runtime Track::call_pattern in crates/audio/src/sequencer.rs (three-entry pattern_return_stack, a fourth nested PATT ends the track), the sequence decoder's Event::Pattern/PatternEnd arms in crates/audio/src/sequence/decode.rs (the depth check in crates/audio/src/sequence/reader.rs runs before the operand read), and the extraction decoder in crates/rom-import/src/domains/song.rs, which expands PATT/PEND inline for the pack and terminates a fourth-level PATT as Fine without reading its pointer.

ply_rept.reason: ply_rept (m4a_1.s:880-910) counts repeats per track: a zero count jumps to the target without touching the counter; a positive count increments first, jumps while the counter is below the count, and resets to zero after the final pass, falling through without using the target. Reimplemented twice: the runtime Track::repeat in crates/audio/src/sequencer.rs (lines 216-228, citing m4a_1.s:880-910), and the sequence decoder's Event::Repeat arm in crates/audio/src/sequence/decode.rs (lines 116-131), which keeps the same counter and validates the target only when the repeat is taken.

LoadMapFromWarp's ClearTempFieldEventData (overworld.c:848) is modelled on this same landing path (issue #248): warp_to clears the temp flag/var ranges on its cloned event data ahead of run_on_transition_map_script, matching upstream's :848-before-:860 (RunOnTransitionMapScript) ordering that Route 103's VAR_OBJ_GFX_ID_0 rival-sprite setup depends on.

CB2_ContinueSavedGame.reason: Resuming a loaded save is OverworldPhase::continue_saved_game: LoadSaveblockMapHeader's location -> map resolution, placement at gSaveBlock1Ptr->pos, the saved player object's current/previous elevation pair (a save whose player object is neither port-marked nor a pristine upstream record (see load_save.c#SaveObjectEvents), or whose current elevation the landing cell could not hold, falls back to the destination tile's own elevation with ObjectEventUpdateElevation's multi-level -> transition substitution), and the saved facing and the saved party. The facing and elevations come from the restored player object event exactly as upstream's ordinary continue path produces it (LoadGameSave -> CopyPartyAndObjectsFromSave -> LoadObjectEvents refills gObjectEvents, then CB2_ReturnToField -> ReturnToFieldLocal -> InitObjectEventsReturnToField -> SpawnObjectEventsOnReturnToField respawns from it); see load_save.c#SaveObjectEvents for how much of that array is modelled. A save block holding DIR_NONE there still falls back to the tile-derived GetAdjustedInitialDirection (overworld.c:929-951 -- shared local-map-load code reached from every warp via InitObjectEventsLocal, not the continue-game-warp branch's own; modelled as engine::overworld::warp_in_facing). The party lead is decoded from the first usable slot across all six stored records when the stored party count is nonzero -- party::select_active_battler's port of SetBattlePartyIds's scan (battle_controllers.c#SetBattlePartyIds), recorded in party::LoadedLead::slot -- rather than re-derived from the provisional starter (load_save.c#CopyPartyAndObjectsToSave). The scan itself is upstream parity (all six slots, matching SetBattlePartyIds's own count-blind sweep, battle_controllers.c:585-606). The one deliberate divergence is the zero-count early return: a stored count of zero short-circuits before that scan and resumes with no lead, where upstream's sweep would still select a valid residual slot. The save side is not divergent, since copy_party_and_objects_to_save (load_save.c#CopyPartyAndObjectsToSave) leaves a no-lead slot's bytes and count exactly as loaded, matching SavePlayerParty's unconditional copy (load_save.c:160-168). Modelled: the continue-game warp branch (:1739-1745). A save whose SaveBlock2.specialSaveWarpFlags carries CONTINUE_GAME_WARP (UseContinueGameWarp, load_save.c:134-137) has that bit alone cleared (ClearContinueGameWarpStatus, load_save.c:139-142) and lands at SaveBlock1.continue_game_warp through OverworldPhase::warp_to_saved_location (SetWarpDestinationToContinueGameWarp -> WarpIntoMap, LoadMapFromWarp's ClearTempFieldEventData (:848) and the supported on-transition effects only, not the full script chain); an unflagged continue keeps the InitMapFromSavedGame-equivalent restore. NOT modelled: TryPutTodaysRivalTrainerOnAir (also run by the else branch, so not warp-specific), and transition scripts beyond warp_to_saved_location's existing coverage. gSaveBlock2Ptr->specialSaveWarpFlags's CONTINUE_GAME_WARP bit that UseContinueGameWarp (load_save.c:134-137) tests is set only by two entry points -- SetContinueGameWarpStatus (load_save.c:144-147), called once, from post_battle_event_funcs.c's GameClear (:36) alongside SetContinueGameWarpToHealLocation (:39,41) on beating the Elite Four; and SetContinueGameWarpStatusToDynamicWarp (load_save.c:149-153), called from seven save-sharing sites -- save.c:1002 (Task_LinkFullSave), start_menu.c:1297 (Task_SaveAfterLinkBattle), trade.c:4714, union_room_chat.c:1570, frontier_util.c:2431 (SaveGameFrontier), record_mixing.c:1004, and contest_util.c:618. Under v1.0.0.0 = the complete single-player game (docs/acceptance/v1.md), two of those eight call sites are in-scope single-player content: GameClear's Hall of Fame (C-1) and SaveGameFrontier (Battle Frontier, C-4, whose frontier_util.c:2431 call is unguarded -- an ordinary solo Frontier save reaches it). So the setters are reachable single-player behaviour that are not implemented yet -- revisit at the Elite Four/Champion milestone, the first point at which a save this port produces can carry the flag; until then only an imported save carries it. The other six sites stay excluded as multiplayer-only, per docs/acceptance/v1.md's exclusion rule: Task_LinkFullSave, Task_SaveAfterLinkBattle, trade, Union Room chat, record mixing, and the Contest Hall save -- contest_util.c:618 sits inside Task_ShowContestResults' `if (gLinkContestFlags & LINK_CONTEST_FLAG_IS_LINK)` branch (contest_util.c:596), so only a link contest ever reaches it and a lone player's Contest Hall run never does. Those exclusions are recorded here rather than assumed, and stand unless single-player play turns out to reach shared upstream behaviour behind them. LoadSaveblockObjEventScripts; DoTimeBasedEvents; PlayTimeCounter_Start; InitMatchCallCounters; ResetSafariZoneFlag_; ResetWinStreaks on SAVE_STATUS_ERROR; LoadSavedMapView; and the Battle Pyramid/Trainer Hill floor special cases are also not modelled.

CB2_WhiteOut.reason: overworld.c:1550-1570. The 120-frame fade-to-black counter, DoMapLoadLoop's map-load state machine, and FieldCB_WarpExitFadeFromBlack's fade-in are not modelled -- this port has no frame-counted fade transition for any warp, matching every other warp/connection crossing's own instant rebind (OverworldPhase::warp_to/warp_to_position/warp_to_saved_location/cross_connection, none of which animate a transition either). Nor is anything else this callback does around the fade: FieldClearVBlankHBlankCallbacks (:1556), StopMapMusic (:1557), and ResetSafariZoneFlag_ (:1558) have no counterparts -- no vblank/hblank callback table is modelled, no map music is playing to stop (crate::music drives the title screen only), and no Safari Zone state exists (though its own persistent flag, FLAG_SYS_SAFARI_MODE, is cleared by DoWhiteOut's own reset -- see src/overworld.c#DoWhiteOut). Of the seven calls upstream makes at the end of the 120 frames, exactly one has a port counterpart that runs: DoWhiteOut (:1559) is OverworldPhase::white_out (see src/overworld.c#DoWhiteOut), called synchronously and immediately, the instant the losing battle's driver reports BattleOutcome::PlayerLost, with no fade in between. The three after it -- ResetInitialPlayerAvatarState (:1560), ScriptContext_Init (:1561), UnlockPlayerFieldControls (:1562) -- run nothing here: this port stores no pre-warp avatar state to reset (see src/overworld.c#GetAdjustedInitialDirection on the missing StoreInitialPlayerAvatarState), has no script engine to re-init, and never locks field controls in the first place (LockPlayerFieldControls is already recorded as unmodelled on src/battle_setup.c#BattleSetup_StartWildBattle), so the map-load-into-overworld handoff white_out performs is just OverworldPhase::warp_to_saved_location's ordinary one (issue #951: the saved-location warp, not the explicit-coordinate warp_to_position). Field poison is a second caller of OverworldPhase::white_out: a four-step drain that faints the last member with HP left reaches it synchronously from the step that drained it (see src/field_poison.c#TryFieldPoisonWhiteOut), with the same absent fade.

DoWhiteOut.reason: overworld.c:358-366. Ordering reproduced exactly: SetMoney(&gSaveBlock1Ptr->money, GetMoney(&gSaveBlock1Ptr->money) / 2) is self.save1.money /= 2 (plain unsigned integer division, no rounding); HealPlayerParty() is, since issue #800 (I-6), a full loop over every occupied saved slot: the selected slot heals through battle::BattlePokemon::heal on the phase's one live battler (the party::LoadedLead) when that slot is within the stored count (or the count is still zero, an unsaved new game where slot 0 is the whole live party), and every other occupied slot heals through a decode/heal/merge round trip on its own saved bytes (party::from_save_pokemon/party::merge_into_save_pokemon) -- see src/script_pokemon_util.c#HealPlayerParty. A selected lead beyond a nonzero stored count is not an occupied slot HealPlayerParty's own count-bounded loop would reach, so it merges its current, un-healed battle state back instead (issue #1241). party::select_active_battler is then re-run against all six stored records when the stored count is nonzero (not just the healed, occupied-count-bounded subset -- SetBattlePartyIds's own rescan is over all PARTY_SIZE slots, so a trailing slot beyond the stored count can still hold a real, decodable Pokemon, issue #1241; a clamped stored count of zero skips this rescan entirely and keeps the previously selected lead, the same zero-means-no-lead contract issue #353 established for continue), since an earlier slot the continue-time scan skipped as fainted may now be the first usable one; Overworld_ResetStateAfterWhiteOut's persistent portion (issue #847) is now EventData::clear_white_out_state -- clears FLAG_SYS_CYCLING_ROAD/_CRUISE_MODE/_SAFARI_MODE/_USE_STRENGTH/_USE_FLASH and, when VAR_SHOULD_END_ABNORMAL_WEATHER == 1, zeroes it and VAR_ABNORMAL_WEATHER_LOCATION -- run unconditionally before destination resolution, so a heal location that fails to resolve does not suppress it; SetWarpDestinationToLastHealLocation() + WarpIntoMap() together are self.warp_to_saved_location(map, heal_location) (issue #951: the complete saved WarpData, warp id included, not just map/x/y), map resolved from self.save1.last_heal_location via saved_map_id -- see src/overworld.c#SetWarpDestinationToLastHealLocation and src/overworld.c#WarpIntoMap. NOT modelled: RunScriptImmediately(EventScript_WhiteOut) -- the Elite Four reset and Mr. Briney relocation this port has no state for, and no 'You blacked out!' message box, since this port has no such content bundled and no message layer wired to this path (see data/event_scripts.s#EventScript_WhiteOut); ResetInitialPlayerAvatarState's avatar-transition state this port has no counterpart for. Called from all three battle-loss drivers via the shared OverworldPhase::white_out (module docs' 'RNG stream' section: draws nothing, matching upstream) -- flow::wild_encounter's advance_wild_battle_frame (CB2_EndWildBattle's IsPlayerDefeated branch, src/battle_setup.c:602-616), flow::overworld_phase::route103_rival_trigger's advance_route103_rival_battle_frame (CB2_EndTrainerBattle's, :1333-1338), and flow::overworld_phase::sight_trainer_trigger's advance_sight_trainer_battle_frame (the same CB2_EndTrainerBattle branch, issue #264), each on BattleOutcome::PlayerLost.

GetAdjustedInitialDirection.reason: Destination-tile branches rewritten as engine::overworld::warp::warp_in_facing, keyed on the arrival tile's metatile behavior exactly as upstream keys on GetCenterScreenMetatileBehavior after WarpIntoMap (flow::OverworldPhase::warp_to reads that behavior off the destination map's runtime and passes it in): deep-south-warp -> North (tested first, before the door arm that also matches it), non-anim-door/door -> South, south-arrow -> North, north-arrow -> South, west-arrow -> East, east-arrow -> West, else South. Three branches are NOT modelled and all collapse into that final else: the FLAG_SYS_CRUISE_MODE + MAP_TYPE_OCEAN_ROUTE branch (no event-flag state), the surfing<->underwater transition branch (no surf/dive avatar flags), and the MetatileBehavior_IsLadder branch that preserves the pre-warp facing (no StoreInitialPlayerAvatarState equivalent -- that function and GetAdjustedInitialTransitionFlags stay unported).

IncrementGameStat.reason: Partially modeled as GameStats::increment: the stored word plus one, saturating at 0xFFFFFF, and a stored value already past the ceiling reads back as exactly 0xFFFFFF (overworld.c:433-445). It is reachable only for the GameStat slots the enum names (SavedGame, FirstHofPlayTime, Steps, EnteredHof, PokemonTrades, link and contest slots, CheckedPokedex); the remaining NUM_USED_GAME_STATS indices (e.g. GAME_STAT_TOTAL_BATTLES) have no variant yet and are added with their producers. The first producer is OverworldPhase::step bumping GameStat::Steps (GAME_STAT_STEPS, slot 5, game_stat.h:9) on each completed, non-forced step.

LoadMapFromCameraTransition.reason: Connection-crossing map switch (issue #177): OverworldPhase::cross_connection models the location/scene core -- SetWarpDestination(mapGroup, mapNum, WARP_ID_NONE, -1, -1) + ApplyCurrentWarp (overworld.c:633, :540-:546, save1.location's exact shape), LoadCurrentMapData (scene/map_id rebind), and RunOnTransitionMapScript (:807, the bounded 2-map transcription in run_on_transition_map_script) -- atomically after PlayerState::step commits the translated position, with a fail-closed restore of the pre-step stance if the rebind is refused. InitSecondaryTilesetAnimation (:815) is modelled as a deliberate no-op: it resets only sSecondaryTilesetAnimCounter (tileset_anims.c:581-583), and this port animates only the primary counter (OverworldPhase::tick), which therefore keeps running across a crossing -- LoadMapFromCameraTransition never calls InitTilesetAnimations (that function's call sites are the full map-load paths: InitMapView overworld.c:529 and the stepped loaders :1867/:1942/:2039). The pixel-precision CameraMove/GetIncomingConnection trigger (:603-:624) is deliberately simplified to grid-step resolution (documented on resolve_connection). NOT modelled, deferred with the systems they belong to: TransitionMapMusic, ResetCyclingRoadChallengeData (:799), TryUpdateRandomTrainerRematches, DoTimeBasedEvents, SetSavedWeatherFromCurrMapHeader, ChooseAmbientCrySpecies (:804), SetDefaultFlashLevel, Overworld_ClearSavedMusic (:806), LoadObjEventTemplatesFromHeader, TrySetMapSaveWarpStatus, InitMap, the secondary tileset/palette copy path (CopySecondaryTilesetToVramUsingHeap/CopySecondaryTilesetPaletteUsingHeap and the ApplyWeatherColorMapToPal(NUM_PALS_IN_PRIMARY..NUM_PALS_TOTAL) loop), DoCurrentWeather (:818), ResetFieldTasksArgs (:819), roamer updates, RunOnResumeMapScript, and ShowMapNamePopup. Stubbed until those land. ClearTempFieldEventData (:798) is no longer deferred: issue #248's Route 103 rival slice wires it into cross_connection (connections.rs), which clears the temp flag/var ranges on its cloned event data ahead of run_on_transition_map_script -- matching upstream's :798-before-:807 ordering -- so Route 103's temp-flag-hidden cuttable trees (FLAG_TEMP_12/_13) reset on every crossing. RestartWildEncounterImmunitySteps (:800) is no longer deferred: issue #169 wires it into cross_connection, so crossing Littleroot's north edge into Route 101 buys the same four encounter-free steps upstream grants.  The live object events are left in place as upstream leaves them: OverworldPhase::cross_connection carries the departed visit's active entries into the entered map's coordinates (ObjectEventCollection::carry_across_connection) instead of reseeding, and the entered map's templates enter unadmitted for the scheduler to admit. The entered scene binds the sprite sheets and palettes of the carried objects as well as its own events' (OverworldScene::from_pack_carrying), so a carried object keeps drawing; object-owned tall-grass effects cross with their owners (OverworldScene::carry_tall_grass_from).

OverworldBasic.reason: OverworldPhase::advance_object_events is the AnimateSprites half (:1468) for object events only: after the frame's input and script work it runs one frame of the live collection's scheduler with the field RNG, frozen while a dialog, a sight-trainer approach, a start menu or a battle owns the field. OverworldPhase::step and an open start menu's frame call it. Not modelled: RunTasks, the camera and panning updates, OAM building and the palette fade, and sprite callbacks other than object events' and the tall-grass effect's (UpdateTallGrassFieldEffect, ported in crates/pokeemerald-rs/src/overworld/grass.rs and run after them). An open start menu's frame (OverworldPhase::advance_start_menu_frame) runs the same sprite order as step: the menu tick (a task, RunTasks :1468) first, then object events, then the tall-grass effect update (the order of step; pinned by the_menu_closing_frame_runs_object_events_before_the_effect_update in crates/pokeemerald-rs/src/flow/overworld_phase/tall_grass_tests/npc.rs), so the callbacks that resume on the frame a menu closes reach that frame's effect update.

Only the two call sites this port's bundled content actually reaches are modelled, as fixed constants rather than a general id-keyed lookup: crate::new_game::default_last_heal_location reproduces InsideOfTruck_EventScript_SetIntroFlagsMale/_Female's own setrespawn HEAL_LOCATION_LITTLEROOT_TOWN_BRENDANS_HOUSE_2F/_MAYS_HOUSE_2F calls (data/maps/InsideOfTruck/scripts.inc:25,38 -- see data/maps/InsideOfTruck#InsideOfTruck_EventScript_SetIntroFlags) at new-game init, cross-checked against src/data/heal_locations.json's own x=4,y=2 entries and the generated assets::MapHeaderTable position for each house (crate::new_game::tests::default_heal_locations_match_the_generated_map_header_positions). The bound is deliberate and narrow, the same 'as much of the chain as this slice runs, no more' posture flow::overworld_phase::first_battle_trigger's own module docs already take for VAR_ROUTE101_STATE.

SetPlayerCoordsFromWarp.reason: overworld.c:603-624 (private upstream, called only from WarpIntoMap). Its warpId>=0 branch was previously unreached by any port caller -- warp_to_position always wrote warp_id: -1 -- so this sub-artifact records issue #951's fix: the new free function saved_warp_position (connections.rs), called from OverworldPhase::warp_to_saved_location, tries a valid destination.warp_id (0 <= id < events.warp_events.len()) against warp_destination_position first, then a non-negative destination.x/.y directly via MapRuntime::arrival_elevation, then the destination map's own center tile (layout.width/2, layout.height/2) as upstream's own last resort for a WarpData with neither -- unreachable through any WarpData this port's own writers produce today (crate::new_game::default_last_heal_location's worst case is an all-zero, non-negative WarpData::default()), but modelled for the same 'honest fallback for corrupt save data' reasoning OverworldPhase::warp_to documents for its own unresolvable cases.

SetWarpData.reason: map_group/map_num/warp_id/x/y field assignment transcribed as the engine::save::WarpData literal OverworldPhase::warp_to builds for save1.location on a resolved warp (flow/overworld_phase/connections.rs); x/y are left at -1 matching SetWarpDestinationToMapWarp's own -1,-1 call shape for a map-warp-id destination (not fixed coordinates). The warp landing that consumes this data also performs LoadMapFromWarp's ClearTempFieldEventData (overworld.c:848) before RunOnTransitionMapScript (:860) -- recorded on ApplyCurrentWarp, same rust_target.

SetWarpDestinationToLastHealLocation.reason: overworld.c:665-668: sWarpDestination = gSaveBlock1Ptr->lastHealLocation, a plain copy of the complete WarpData, warp id included. OverworldPhase::white_out reads self.save1.last_heal_location and resolves its (map_group, map_num) through saved_map_id (crates/pokeemerald-rs/src/flow/overworld_phase.rs, shared with SaveBlock1::location's own CB2_ContinueSavedGame resolution) to hand warp_to_saved_location a real assets::MapId plus the whole saved WarpData -- this port's 'destination' is computed on demand rather than staged through a separate sWarpDestination global (oop-boundaries: no global mutable state), but the value copied, including warp_id, is the same one (issue #951: an earlier revision forwarded only map/x/y and rewrote warp_id to -1).

WarpIntoMap.reason: overworld.c:626-631: ApplyCurrentWarp (copy sWarpDestination into gSaveBlock1Ptr->location verbatim), LoadCurrentMapData, SetPlayerCoordsFromWarp (:603-624, see src/overworld.c#SetPlayerCoordsFromWarp for its own three branches). OverworldPhase::warp_to_position remains the WARP_ID_NONE-shaped explicit-coordinate counterpart for its one remaining caller, the scripted first-battle conclusion's literal warp command, which has no warp id or saved WarpData to consult. The white-out's heal-location caller (issue #951) now goes through OverworldPhase::warp_to_saved_location instead, which honors a saved warp_id when present -- see src/overworld.c#SetPlayerCoordsFromWarp. Both helpers land at the destination tile's own elevation (issue #379), not the ELEVATION_TRANSITION wildcard (0, include/global.fieldmap.h:16) InitPlayerAvatar seeds a fresh avatar with: they read the landing cell off the destination map's decoded grid through engine::overworld::MapRuntime::arrival_elevation, applying ObjectEventUpdateElevation's own multi-level -> ELEVATION_TRANSITION substitution (event_object_movement.c:7759-7771 -- see that file's ObjectEventUpdateElevation entry). Upstream overwrites the sentinel on the spawn frame itself, before input unlocks (triggerGroundEffectsOnMove -> DoGroundEffects_OnSpawn -> UpdateObjectEventElevationAndPriority), so the sentinel is never observable at rest and both helpers share the one arrival read warp_destination_position and the continue-game placement already use. warp_to_saved_location writes save1.location with the saved WarpData verbatim, warp id included; warp_to_position keeps writing the heal/warp coordinates with warp_id -1 (ApplyCurrentWarp's plain copy, again).

sOverworldBgTemplates.reason: BG0-3 index/priority assignment for the overworld's bottom/middle/top metatile layers, transcribed as viewport::{TOP,MIDDLE,BOTTOM}_{BG_INDEX,PRIORITY} consts; BG0 (weather/other overlay effects) is out of this slice's scope and stays unbound.

Bgr555ToRgb888.reason: Bgr555::to_rgb888 ports the BGR555->RGB888 5-to-8-bit channel expansion ((c<<3)|(c>>2)), verified against mgba's gl.c normalized /31. reference; the rest of palette.c (fades, blending) is out of scope for this slice (issue #50).

color_effect_blend.reason: effects::alpha_blend/brighten/darken port the hardware BLDALPHA/BLDY per-pixel color-effect math -- the same per-channel weighted-lerp-over-16 formula BlendPalette (util.c) uses for CPU palette fades, generalized to the two-independent-weight (EVA/EVB) form and operating on the compositor's live per-pixel layer stack rather than a static palette buffer, verified against mgba's mColorMix5Bit/_brighten/_darken as compiled for stock desktop mGBA (SDL/Qt) -- the non-COLOR_16_BIT, 8-bit-per-channel path (mgba/include/mgba-util/image.h:15-20, 253-266, 307-327; mgba/src/gba/renderers/software-private.h:237-245, 270-278), since COLOR_16_BIT is only ever defined for the Wii/3DS/libretro build targets (mgba/src/platform/wii/CMakeLists.txt:11, mgba/src/platform/3ds/CMakeLists.txt:14, mgba/CMakeLists.txt:1026), never desktop, and docs/acceptance/v1.md's binding gate is the observable experience on mGBA (docs/principles.md's reference-only). Those three routines mask each channel in place in the packed u32, so _darken's shifted (green/blue) lanes subtract ceil(c*y/16) where its low (red) lane subtracts floor(c*y/16) -- _darken(0xFFFFFF, 7) is (144, 143, 143) -- and darken_red_channel/darken_shifted_channel reproduce both, pinned by an exhaustive oracle test over every 5-bit channel value and every usable EVY (S-2 slice 4, issue #99; corrected to the 32-bit oracle in issue #380). The rest of palette.c (BeginNormalPaletteFade/UpdatePaletteFade's CPU fade sequencing, TintPalette_GrayScale/_SepiaTone, InvertPlttBuffer) remains pending -- distinct software palette-buffer features, not this hardware register path. OBJWIN-masked forced-alpha composition selects a target-1 BG's brighten/darken variant (effects::objwin_bg_variant) when the OBJWIN region enables effects, before mixing it as the immediate target 2, while unmasked forced-alpha BG neighbors stay normal (mgba/src/gba/renderers/software-private.h:87-125,156-171); pinned for regular and affine BGs by crates/rendering/src/compositor/tests/objwin.rs (issue #1794).

normal_palette_fade.reason: palette_fade::NormalPaletteFade reimplements the front-end NORMAL_FADE subset of BeginNormalPaletteFade (palette.c:156-199) and UpdatePaletteFade normal-mode dispatch (palette.c:114-131) plus UpdateNormalPaletteFade BG/OBJ scheduler (palette.c:406-490) and the four-then-done finishing polls (palette.c:807-828), fixed to PALETTES_ALL, zero delay, deltaY=2, and a black or white target. begin() fades 0->16 and begin_in() fades 16->0 (yDec, palette.c:177-184,454-475; used by option_menu.c:250), both running the immediate first update the way BeginNormalPaletteFade calls UpdatePaletteFade before returning; update() alternates background/object halves, stepping the coefficient only once both halves of a pair have processed, and reports Active for exactly four finishing polls before Done, pinned by status-trace tests. Palette masks other than all, nonzero delay, start/target coefficients other than 0->16 and 16->0, FAST_FADE/HARDWARE_FADE, palette-buffer/PLTT transfer machinery, PaletteStruct behavior, TintPalette_GrayScale/_SepiaTone/_CustomTone, InvertPlttBuffer, and the rest of palette.c remain pending; flow-level wiring that holds a scene through the fade is issue #1329 and the Options screen owner, not this artifact. The composition side: OverworldScene::compose_live applies a PaletteStage at palette-sample time through rendering::FrameEffects::palette so BG and OBJ blend before composition (the point UpdatePaletteFade's buffer transfer feeds, palette.c:114-131), and the dialog, start menu and bag overlays are staged per bank by crate::palette_overlay::stage_overlay (crates/pokeemerald-rs/src/palette_overlay.rs), which replays a painter on black and white frames and maps exactly the pixels it wrote. The stage is identity by default; the flow states that run a real fade (FadeScreen, field_weather.c:737-759,781-795; SetupBagMenu's fade-in, item_menu.c:770-775) remain #2909's.

CursorCb_TakeItem.reason: Models the effect and the outcome messages: CursorCb_TakeItem (party_menu.c:3273-3298) takes the held item through TryTakeMonItem. The menu offers TAKE ITEM only for a non-mail holder (a mail holder gets CursorCb_TakeMail instead, SetPartyMonFieldSelectionActions, party_menu.c:2631-2634, ItemIsMail at mail_data.c:185), so party::take_held_item refuses a mail holder untouched (HoldsMail) as a stand-in for that menu construction. OverworldPhase::show_take_item_outcome is the flow hook, for the lead only, called by the start menu's TAKE entry (StartMenuItem::TakeItem, a stand-in for the party menu's ITEM then TAKE path): it stages the take on copies of the lead's battler and the bag (OverworldPhase::stage_take_lead_held_item), opens the outcome's message box, and only then commits (OverworldPhase::commit_take_lead_held_item), which moves the staged battler and bag into place and merges the lead into the save only when the item moved; a box that cannot be built commits nothing. It shows the outcome in the field message box (flow/overworld_phase/take_item_message.rs), which holds field input until dismissed: gText_PkmnNotHolding for NotHolding, BufferBagFullCantTakeItemMessage's gText_BagFullCouldNotRemoveItem for BagFull, and DisplayTookHeldItemMessage's gText_ReceivedItemFromPkmn for Took, with GetMonNickname (the record's nickname) as STR_VAR_1 and CopyItemName as STR_VAR_2. CalculateBaseDamage.reason: Partial: the level/power/atk-def core plus the in-function burn, Reflect/Light-Screen, and weather hooks are rewritten as base_damage. Burn (STATUS1_BURN) halves a physical attacker's damage after the division by 50 unless the attacker has Guts (pokemon.c:3262-3264): crate::ability::burn_halves_damage derives DamageInput::attacker_burned from the attacker's Status1::Burned and ability, read by hit::damage_input, trainer_ai::estimated_damage and suitability::stale_base_damage so the hit pipeline, the AI estimate and the forced-replacement selector agree; Special moves are never halved. The confusion self-hit passes the same attacker_burned (crate::battle::execute::Battle::apply_self_hit reads burn_halves_damage on the confused battler, who is both attacker and defender in the call), so a burned non-Guts battler's self-hit is halved after the division by 50 exactly as an ordinary hit is. The pinch-ability power boost at :3219-:3226 is modelled -- gBattleMovePower = (150 * gBattleMovePower) / 100 when the move's type matches the attacker's Overgrow/Blaze/Torrent/Swarm and hp <= maxHP / 3 -- applied to the POWER before the formula reads it (DamageInput::attacker_pinch_boost, crate::ability::pinch_boosts_power), so the truncation lands where upstream puts it. Only Overgrow is reachable in a battle this crate can construct; the other three rows are carried because they are the same four consecutive upstream lines. The Huge Power / Pure Power attack doubling at :3158-:3159 is modelled -- attack *= 2 whenever a physical move's attacker carries either ability, applied to the RAW stat before APPLY_STAT_MOD's stat-stage scaling at :3238-:3244 (crate::ability::huge_power_attack, read by both hit::damage_before_roll and the trainer AI's AI_CalcDmg estimate so the two agree). Guts and Marvel Scale's own status1 reads at :3211-:3214 are modelled -- attack = (150 * attack) / 100 for a statused Guts holder's physical Attack and defense = (150 * defense) / 100 for a statused Marvel Scale holder's physical Defense, each truncated and applied to the RAW stat before the same APPLY_STAT_MOD stage scaling (crate::ability::guts_attack, crate::ability::marvel_scale_defense, read directly by BattlePokemon::attacking_stat/defending_stat so hit::damage_before_roll and the trainer AI's estimate agree here too). Hustle's attack boost at :3205-:3206 is modelled -- attack = (150 * attack) / 100 for a Hustle holder's physical Attack, truncated and applied to the RAW stat before the same APPLY_STAT_MOD stage scaling (crate::ability::hustle_attack, read directly by BattlePokemon::attacking_stat so hit::damage_before_roll, the trainer AI's estimate, and the forced-replacement suitability selector's stale base damage all agree). The confusion self-hit's own call -- CalculateBaseDamage(&gBattleMons[gBattlerAttacker], &gBattleMons[gBattlerAttacker], MOVE_POUND, 0, 40, 0, ...) at battle_util.c:2159 -- is modelled: crate::battle::execute::Battle::apply_self_hit reads BattlePokemon::attacking_stat/defending_stat on the same battler for both the attack and defense side, with power 40 and Type::Normal (MOVE_POUND's type) and no critical override, so the shared Hustle/Guts/Marvel Scale/Huge Power hooks above apply symmetrically to the self-hit exactly as they do to an ordinary hit; the pinch-ability boost is hardcoded false since Normal typing never matches its Fire/Water/Grass/Bug gate, and sideStatus is hardcoded 0 upstream so Reflect never applies here either, matching this crate's own reflect: false. The same call also models the Explosion defense-halving at pokemon.c:3228-3230 (defense /= 2 when gBattleMoves[gCurrentMove].effect == EFFECT_EXPLOSION, applied to the raw Defense before the APPLY_STAT_MOD stage scaling at :3248-:3260): the confusion branch passes MOVE_POUND as an argument (battle_util.c:2173) but the test reads gCurrentMove, the attempted move, so crate::battle::execute::Battle::apply_self_hit takes that move and halves BattlePokemon::defending_stat's raw Defense when its MoveData::effect is MoveEffect::EXPLOSION (Selfdestruct and Explosion), keeping power 40, the variance draw, and no PP spent. A depleted slot qualifies because wild selection redraws only MOVE_NONE and AtkCanceler_UnableToUseMove runs ahead of Cmd_attackcanceler's no-PP abort. Thick Fat's raw Special Attack halving at :3202-:3204 (Fire/Ice against a Thick Fat defender, truncated and applied before stage scaling) is modelled (crate::ability::thick_fat_special_attack), applied after the Huge Power / Pure Power doubling and before stage scaling by hit::damage_input, trainer_ai::estimated_damage and suitability::stale_base_damage, so the hit pipeline, the AI estimate, the admitted Icicle Spear multi-hit loop and the selector agree. Plus and Minus at :3207-:3210 are modelled -- a Plus holder with Minus on the field, or a Minus holder with Plus, has raw Special Attack raised by (150 * spAttack) / 100, truncated and applied before stage scaling; upstream's field scan at battle_util.c:3128-3137 has no side or HP filter, so the single-battle opposing active mon counts (crate::ability::plus_minus_special_attack, read by hit::damage_input, trainer_ai::estimated_damage, and suitability::stale_base_damage). Still pending from the same function: hold-item boosts, the other ability modifiers (Flash Fire), badge boosts, Explosion defense-halving for an ordinary hit (the Selfdestruct/Explosion execution pipeline is unported, so only the confusion self-hit reaches it), Mud/Water Sport field sports, and double-battle spread/screen variants. The surrounding STAB/type/roll battle-script steps are tracked under src/battle_script_commands.c. CalculateMonStats.reason: pokemon.c:2814 (CALC_STAT macro), 2823 (CalculateMonStats), 2845-2848 (Shedinja's flat 1 max HP). The max-HP and CALC_STAT formulas are modelled (compute_stats/calc_stat/calc_max_hp), fed real EVs -- BattlePokemon::with_evs adopts a loaded record's own retained EV bytes at construction; see src/pokemon.c#MonGainEVs for how BattlePokemon::evs is populated in-battle. The persisted stat cache is BattlePokemon::cached_stats, the raw Normal Forme block (never Deoxys's Speed Forme view, which only the live BattlePokemon::stats carries; see src/pokemon.c#GetDeoxysStat). Loading: BattlePokemon::with_cached_stats adopts a loaded record's stat block and current HP verbatim, neither recomputed, clamped nor normalised, and BattlePokemon::with_saved_experience adopts the experience word without moving the level or any stat, because upstream's LoadPlayerParty copies the record and calls nothing (load_save.c:160-178); party::from_save_pokemon calls both, so a record whose level byte, experience word, EVs and cache disagree stays exactly as saved until its next level-up, and a loaded mon keeps its stored HP and stats rather than being rebuilt from the formula. Saving: party::to_save_pokemon and party::merge_into_save_pokemon write BattlePokemon::cached_stats and the live HP back unchanged -- no recompute, no hidden-HP offset, no evs_at_last_level_up snapshot -- so Continue then SAVE is byte-exact and repeated saves file the same bytes. Level-up: BattlePokemon::raise_level_to_experience (reached in production only from apply_experience; the test-only reconcile_saved_experience shares it) replaces the whole cache with compute_stats_with_evs at the EVs the mon then holds, as Cmd_getexp does after the KO's MonGainEVs (battle_script_commands.c:3420,3465-3478), and applies the HP rule of pokemon.c:2866-2895 (hp_after_recalculation) against the cache's previous maximum: a fainted mon stays at 0, a living Shedinja is set to 1, any other living mon moves by the signed newMaxHP - oldMaxHP, stored through the 16-bit HP field unclamped as stock upstream does with BUGFIX off (pokemon.c:2882-2895), so a non-positive result wraps (the Pomeg glitch) and a zero result faints. A zero HP over a zero old maximum is an uninitialised mon (pokemon.c:2875-2878): a non-Shedinja takes the new maximum and Shedinja takes 1. Gaining EVs does not recompute the cache (BattlePokemon::gain_evs): only the next level-up reads the EVs, as upstream does. calc_max_hp forces max HP to 1 for SPECIES_SHEDINJA before the ordinary formula runs, at every stat-computation site. A cached block adopted verbatim may hold a zero maximum or HP above the maximum; the trainer and opponent AI HP-percentage reads floor the denominator at 1, and the drain and absorbing-ability heal reports saturate at zero. Still not modelled: evolution, vitamins, and Box withdrawal as CalculateMonStats call sites.

CalculatePPWithBonus.reason: pokemon.c:4650-:4654, plus the gPPUpGetMask/gPPUpClearMask tables it reads (:1857-:1866). Fully modelled (issue #304) as battle::pokemon::pp_bonuses: PpBonuses is upstream's packed ppBonuses byte (two bits per move slot, struct PokemonSubstruct0::ppBonuses at include/pokemon.h:104 and struct BattlePokemon::ppBonuses at :288) as an owned type, and calculate_pp_with_bonus is basePP + ((basePP * 20 * ppUps) / 100) with upstream's single trailing truncation rather than a per-Up one. BattlePokemon carries the byte whole (not a per-slot field) so the save round trip is byte-exact, including bits belonging to a slot the moveset does not fill; PpBonuses::get is the (gPPUpGetMask[i] & bonuses) >> (2 * i) read and PpBonuses::cleared is gPPUpClearMask's write. Every one of the 256 bytes is accepted -- two-bit fields cannot overflow, so there is nothing to reject. BattlePokemon::max_pp is the per-slot application: it is what HealPlayerParty restores to and the bound a PP Up works against, but not a cap on a saved value -- BattlePokemon::with_saved_pp adopts a saved PP byte above it unchanged, as GetMonData(MON_DATA_PP1 + slot) returns substruct1->pp[slot] with no clamp to that maximum (pokemon.c:3851-:3855), and deduct_pp counts down from the adopted value. The arithmetic runs in u32 and saturates back to u8 where C would wrap, unreachable for real data (the largest gBattleMoves pp is 40, giving 64 fully upgraded). NOT modelled: applying a PP Up at all -- ITEM4_PP_UP's gPPUpAddValues path (:4958-:4972) and the Max Elixir-style :5256-:5264 case need an item-use path this port does not have, so a nonzero byte can only arrive from a save file today.

MonTryLearningNewMove.reason: pokemon.c's level-up move learning (MonTryLearningNewMove, :3014-:3044, and GiveMoveToMon/GiveMoveToBoxMon, :2934-:2955), reached in-battle from Cmd_getexp via BattleScript_LevelUp -> Cmd_handlelearnnewmove (battle_script_commands.c:5360) and in the overworld from the daycare/evolution paths (still not modelled -- see below). As of issue #252, BattlePokemon::apply_experience (walk in crates/battle/src/pokemon/learn.rs) spends the award one level threshold at a time in ascending order, upstream's own consumption shape (Task_GiveExpToMon's cap at nextLvlExp, battle_controller_player.c:1154-:1181, looped by Cmd_getexp case 5), and offers each of that level's assets::LevelUpLearnsets entries, in table order, to GiveMoveToBoxMon's two outcomes: a move already known is skipped at no slot cost (MON_ALREADY_KNOWS_MOVE, :2951-:2952), and a move with an empty slot is learned into it at its own base PP (:2945-:2949, writes at :2947-:2948). Teaching is UNSCREENED, exactly as upstream teaches: whatever move id the learnset names is learned, including one whose effect this crate has no resolver for -- a level-6 Treecko learns Absorb even though EFFECT_ABSORB is unmodelled (crate::hit's module docs). That needs no screen because this path only runs on the PLAYER's mon, and the player's moveset is the one Battle::new documents as deliberately unscreened (only the wild mon is screened at Battle::new, whose rejection loop can land on any slot mid-turn; new_trainer separately screens the trainer's whole party for its own documented bench-arrival reason); a player slot is validated per turn at selection by validate_player_move, ahead of the turn's first RNG draw, and an unexecutable pick is refused with a recoverable BattleError that leaves the battle usable. The four-known-moves case is no longer a divergence: as of issue #304 it is modelled as the pause upstream makes. MON_HAS_MAX_MOVES (:2954) stops the walk and parks a PendingMoveLearn ON THE MON (BattlePokemon::pending_move_learn) -- gMoveToLearn plus the resume position upstream keeps in the sLearningMoveTableID file-static (:3021), owned state exactly as upstream's globals are, so a stale copy cannot be replayed and one mon's prompt cannot be answered on another -- which is upstream reaching BattleScript_AskToLearnMove's yes/no box (battle_script_commands.c:5368-:5370); the pause holds the mon AT the prompted level, the award's remainder unconsumed on the token, so a prompt never exposes prematurely raised levels or stats. Nothing is learned until BattlePokemon::resolve_move_learn is given a MoveLearnDecision, and apply_experience's return is #[must_use] so a caller cannot overlook the open question. Declining resumes the same walk at the next entry exactly as BattleScript_TryLearnMoveLoop does; replacing a slot performs both of Cmd_yesnoboxlearnmove's writes in upstream's order, RemoveMonPPBonus then SetMonMoveSlot (:5479-:5480), so the forgotten move's PP Ups go with it and the incoming move starts at its own base PP. The walk lives in crates/battle/src/pokemon/learn.rs; crates/pokeemerald-rs/src/flow/move_learn.rs is where this port's three headless drivers answer, with the documented stand-in (decline) they use for every other absent player input, since there is no battle scene to ask in. NOT modelled from the replacement path: the yes/no box, the summary-screen move list (ShowSelectMovePokemonSummaryScreen, :5449), and every string. IsHMMove2's refusal to overwrite an HM slot (:5468-:5472) IS modelled -- BattleError::HmMoveCantBeForgotten, refused before any write with the prompt left answerable, because a loaded save (or the unrestricted constructor) can legitimately hold an HM move even though no learnset names one; see src/battle_script_commands.c#Cmd_yesnoboxlearnmove. Pinned in crates/battle/src/pokemon/learn.rs's own tests (pause, decline, replace-clears-the-bonus, resume), crates/battle/tests/turn_engine/trainer_battle.rs (a_full_moveset_asks_before_learning_and_honours_either_answer, a_trainer_battles_exp_award_surfaces_the_replacement_prompt, a_multi_level_jump_learns_each_crossed_levels_moves_in_order) and crates/pokeemerald-rs/src/flow/move_learn/tests.rs (a driver that leaves the prompt unanswered abandons a winnable fight). The overworld Move Reminder/Deleter and evolution move learning remain out of scope. The save decoder deliberately never reaches this walk: from_save_pokemon adopts a stored experience total verbatim through BattlePokemon::with_saved_experience, deriving no level and teaching nothing on load, as upstream's LoadPlayerParty copies the record and calls nothing (load_save.c:160-178); a total that disagrees with the saved level is reconciled only by the next in-battle award through apply_experience, pinned by decoding_an_inconsistent_save_keeps_the_saved_level_and_moves in crates/pokeemerald-rs/src/party/tests/codec.rs. No production path derives a level from saved experience: BattlePokemon::reconcile_saved_experience (a level raise without teaching) is test support only, behind battle's test-support feature, used by unit tests to level a mon without a battle fixture. A move a free slot takes is reported rather than learned silently: BattlePokemon::apply_experience_reporting returns an ExperienceAward whose learned list holds each free-slot move in the order the walk reached it (the walk's push into the moveset is the GiveMoveToBoxMon write at :2947-:2948), alongside the pending prompt when a later entry finds the moveset full. apply_experience is the same walk returning only the prompt. Because a prompt opens only on a full moveset and neither answer frees a slot, resolve_move_learn's resumed walk can only open further prompts and reports no free-slot learns. Pinned by a_free_slot_learns_without_asking_and_reports_the_move, free_slot_learns_across_levels_are_reported_in_learning_order and free_slots_fill_before_a_prompt_and_the_report_keeps_both in crates/battle/src/pokemon/learn.rs.

The player looks screen-fixed upstream (and is drawn at the fixed avatar::PLAYER_OBJ_X/Y here) because its own walk animation advances sprite->x/y by 1px/frame along travel (Step1, src/event_object_movement.c:8191), cancelling the coord offset frame for frame; this port collapses that cancellation to a constant -- see SetSpritePosToMapCoords' own ledger entry.

The rotation/scale-to-matrix computation (ObjAffineSet/SetOamMatrix trig side) is not modelled -- only matrix selection and consumption are. sample_texel's local_x parameter also carries SpriteLayer::sample_affine_local's OBJ-mosaic caller (S-2 issue #802, complements oam_mosaic): a mosaic-enabled affine entry passes a signed footprint-local column that can be -1 (a leading block held one column before the sprite's own edge, mirroring mgba's SPRITE_TRANSFORMED_MOSAIC_LOOP pre-loop seed at source position inX-1, software-obj.c:53,241) or a column past the bounding box (a mosaic-extended trailing block); both resolve through the existing post-transform out-of-source check rather than a separate pre-transform bound. An ObjMode::Window affine entry still reaches this mosaic path but with MosaicSize::vertical_only (crate::mosaic): SpriteLayer::sample_entry_mosaic keeps the vertical row snap mgba applies unconditionally before dispatch (video-software.c:1027,1042-1050) while never holding the transformed position across a horizontal block, matching mgba's unconditional non-mosaic SPRITE_TRANSFORMED_LOOP for FLAG_OBJWIN (software-obj.c:287-288/303-304). Windows/blending otherwise remain out of scope (issue #98).

oam_admission.reason: Not a port of any pokeemerald src/sprite.c function -- pokeemerald itself assumes unlimited per-scanline OAM processing and never models the GBA's fixed OBJ cycle budget. Filed here (alongside affine_oam/oam_mosaic) as the sprite renderer's third mgba-verified hardware-timing artifact: OamAdmission::for_scanline (crate::oam_budget) ports the GBA PPU's real per-scanline OAM admission -- a fixed cycle budget (mgba/include/mgba/internal/gba/video.h:36-37: OBJ_LENGTH=1210 normally, OBJ_HBLANK_FREE_LENGTH=954 when DISPCNT's HBlank-interval-free bit is set, mgba/src/gba/renderers/video-software.c:623) that caps OAM traversal at 128 physical entries (mgba/src/gba/renderers/common.c:13) and drops late sprites/OBJWIN masks once exhausted. sprite_list_cost ports mgba's OAM clean pass (common.c:18-45): an entry that is disabled (common.c:18) or lies entirely off the left edge, x + width < 0 (common.c:34-36 for a regular entry; common.c:43-45, which tests the raw 9-bit X field, rejects an affine one on the same condition), never enters the sprite list at all -- it is neither drawn nor charged its own cost, only the traversal its index contributes. Costs are mgba's two unclipped formulas (common.c:24-39), taken over the entry's bounding-box width (already doubled for AffineDoubleSize per common.c:26): affine 8 + width * 2 then += x when x < 0; regular width - 2 then += x >> 1 when x < 0 (C's arithmetic shift, which Rust's i32 >> reproduces). mgba never clips width to the on-screen part, and the two kinds fall off at different rates: a 64-wide entry costs 62 (regular) / 136 (affine) at x=0, 46 / 104 at x=-32, 30 / 72 at x=-64. The walk itself is video-software.c:1029-1064's charge-then-check ordering: traversal is 2 * (index - lastIndex) with lastIndex starting at 0, so OAM index 0's traversal is free and every later slot costs 2; the charge lands before the exhaustion test; that test is remaining <= 0, not < 0; an off-scanline entry is skipped only after both (video-software.c:1040-1042); and an admitted entry's own cost is deducted only after processing (video-software.c:1064), so a sprite whose own cost crosses zero is still drawn and only the next slot's traversal stops the rest. common.c:43-45's rejection of entries entirely off the *right* edge (x >= 240 -- the raw 9-bit X band 240..=255, which decodes to no visible pixel) is modelled the same way: such a slot retains only the walk's traversal cost and cannot drain the per-scanline budget or displace a later visible sprite (oam_budget.rs's right-edge tests); the case is reachable, snow weather parks wrapped flakes near x = 242 (src/field_weather_effect.c:970). SpriteLayer::resolve_pixel and SpriteLayer::objwin_mask (sprite.rs) both gate their entry iteration through this single admission stage -- reading it out of one per-scanline cache slot (SpriteLayer::with_admission), which both keeps the walk to once per scanline rather than once per pixel per path and makes it structurally impossible for visible resolution and OBJWIN masking to disagree about which entries a scanline exhausted. SpriteLayer::with_hblank_free_interval threads DISPCNT's HBlank-interval-free bit in from the caller -- pokeemerald sets that bit unconditionally in the overworld's DISPCNT setup (src/overworld.c:2122-2123; that file is still ledger-pending overall and this bit is not yet its own tracked artifact), so a future caller wiring live DISPCNT state through gets the reduced 954-cycle budget for free. Issue #329 (S-2).

oam_mosaic.reason: OamEntry::mosaic/with_mosaic port OamData's OBJ mosaic bit. SpriteLayer::resolve_pixel_with_mosaic/objwin_mask_with_mosaic snap a mosaic-enabled Regular entry's sampling coordinate to its MOSAIC-register OBJ block origin (crate::mosaic) before sampling, verified against mgba's SPRITE_MOSAIC_LOOP macro (S-2 slice 4, issue #99). A mosaic-enabled affine entry instead holds the *transformed* source position across a screen-space block (SpriteLayer::sample_affine_local, S-2 issue #802), verified against mgba's distinct SPRITE_TRANSFORMED_MOSAIC_LOOP macro (software-obj.c:49-71, selected at :289-295/:305-311): it rejects an out-of-source position after transforming rather than clamping the bounding-box coordinate before transforming, so a leading partial block can sample outside the nominal texture and stay unwritten, unlike the regular loop's edge clamp. Vertical mosaic snapping stays shared between both dispatch branches (mgba clamps the source scanline identically before either loop runs, video-software.c:1027-1050). SpriteLayer::sample_entry_mosaic keeps only that vertical snap for any ObjMode::Window entry (both Regular and affine) via MosaicSize::vertical_only, matching mgba snapping the source row before dispatch regardless of FLAG_OBJWIN (video-software.c:1027,1042-1050) while selecting the unconditional non-mosaic (non-block-holding) loop horizontally whenever FLAG_OBJWIN is set -- the mosaic-rounded trailing draw condition still applies too, since mgba computes it unconditionally before that dispatch (software-obj.c:233-239 affine, :320-325 regular; loop selection at :344-345/360-361 regular, :287-288/303-304 affine). Complements oam_regular_fields/affine_oam/oam_obj_mode. An affine hold additionally restarts at each hardware-window span's own start rather than only at a mosaic block boundary, porting mgba's per-span sprite preprocessing rerun (software-obj.c:227-242, video-software.c:1052-1062): compose_frame_with_effects (crates/rendering/src/compositor.rs) threads each scanline's window span starts and per-span OBJ-pass eligibility into SpriteLayer::resolve_pixel_with_mosaic_windowed's WindowSpans, whose sample_affine_local seeds a held sample from inX-1 at its own span's start instead of the mosaic block's, and searches later OBJ-drawing spans for a trailing spill the sprite's own raw edge binds past its span, sharing the same same-entry write lock that stops a contested slot's spill search at its first candidate span (software-obj.c:79-85). Separately, an OBJWIN entry's contribution -- opaque or a transparent hole -- is dropped per the *writing* span whose own rank outranks OBJWIN's, not the queried column's (software-obj.c:161, video-software.c:131-134): SpriteLayer::sample_entry_mosaic and sample_affine_local filter candidate spans on WindowSpans::suppresses_objwin/span_suppresses_objwin so a WINOUT pass's OBJWIN hole still promotes a worse-priority OBJ under its trailing spill even where that spill lands inside WIN0/WIN1, which a queried-column-only suppression check would wrongly discard (S-2, issue #1084). objwin_mask_with_mosaic never receives this span state and always samples with WindowSpans::WHOLE_SCANLINE, because OBJWIN is a per-pixel mask rather than a hardware-window span and mgba never restarts a hold for it (S-2, issue #1084). The draw-time brighten/darken variant and FLAG_REBLEND postpass a written OBJ pixel carries are SpritePixel and effects::resolve_pixel_color's concern (S-2, issue #1305), independent of which span the mosaic hold or OBJWIN suppression above resolves.

ClearTextSpan.reason: Issue #1273 ported only the erased rectangle's geometry (Printer::clear_span, text.c:1063-1090's width > 0 guard, gCurGlyph.height per font at text.c:1713,1755,1797,1841,1883); this closes the gap the Rust module's own doc comment flagged: neither consumer painted it. This reproduces upstream's fill-then-continue behaviour. The erase colour is modelled: ClearedSpan carries the TextColors in force, and textbox's Eraser::erase paints text.c:655-673's fill with the span's background -- index 0 (TEXT_COLOR_TRANSPARENT) paints nothing (upstream's sLastTextBgColor skip), the window's interior index (the message box's white 1, B_WIN_MSG's fill 15, passed as textbox::WindowBackdrop::interior) restores the pre-glyph window interior, and any other index fills with that window-palette entry. A FILL_WINDOW or page clear erases the whole content rectangle the same way, with the colours Printer::cleared_window_colors captured (index 0 shows the scene under the window).

NpcDialog, IntroScene and the start menu's message box retain the placement Printer::keypad_icon reports after each tick as a WindowOp::KeypadIcon, so a later CLEAR/CLEAR_TO or window scroll acts on the icon like on a glyph. The naming controls banner also consumes Printer::keypad_icon in crates/pokeemerald-rs/src/naming/compositor/text.rs, copying the same nonzero sheet indices into its indexed WindowBuffer before tile composition.

Audio extended control codes (including the PLAY_* family) and PALETTE are consumed as documented no-ops; FONT, MIN_LETTER_SPACING and the colour controls are modelled, see below; see the module's 'Deliberately out of scope' docs. EXT_CTRL_CODE_PAUSE is no longer among them: it is a modelled render state -- PrinterState::Pause mirrors upstream's RENDER_STATE_PAUSE (text.c:1215-1220), counting the control code's argument frames down before returning to HandleChar. EXT_CTRL_CODE_CLEAR and EXT_CTRL_CODE_CLEAR_TO have left that no-op set too: both keep upstream's width > 0 guard (text.c:1063-1090) -- CLEAR erases its argument's width at the cursor and advances past it, CLEAR_TO erases forward to the origin-relative column and so never moves the cursor back, unlike its sibling SKIP -- and a clear that did erase ends the frame the way upstream's RENDER_PRINT does, while a clear with nothing ahead stays a free RENDER_REPEAT. The erased rectangle is reported through Printer::cleared_span rather than painted; see src/text.c#ClearTextSpan. EXT_CTRL_CODE_FILL_WINDOW has left that no-op set too: it fills the whole window with the background colour and resets both cursor axes to the printer origin before continuing within the same frame as RENDER_REPEAT (text.c:1048-1057), surfaced through Printer::cleared_window rather than painted, same as the CLEAR/CLEAR_TO span above. CHAR_KEYPAD_ICON is modelled too: the icon's placement and cursor advance follow text.c:1114-1118 -- Printer::tick records a KeypadIconPlacement at the cursor (read via Printer::keypad_icon), advances the cursor by the icon's width from keypad_icon_size (the sKeypadIcons table, text.c:98-115), and ends the frame as RENDER_PRINT does (TickEvent::Idle); the printer has no template letter spacing, so the advance is the width alone. The icon bitmap itself is drawn by the dialog and intro compositors; see src/text.c#DrawKeypadIcon. EXT_CTRL_CODE_FONT has left that no-op set too: it is a RENDER_REPEAT-class control (text.c:1007-1010) that changes only the source the next glyph renders from (Printer::active_font), mapping upstream ids as the glyph dispatch does (text.c:1123-1141) -- FONT_SMALL, FONT_NORMAL, FONT_SHORT with FONT_SHORT_COPY_1..3 as Short, FONT_NARROW, FONT_SMALL_NARROW -- while Braille, Bold and unknown ids select no source, so later glyphs are skipped with no fallback glyph.
